glossary.definition: The enterprise-level system providing library data structures and services, including such functions as acquisitions and cataloging.

requirements.name: Material Volume Report
requirements.description: The system shall provide the ability to report on the volume of material in a given Library at any point in time. For a selected Library, the system shall report the count of new acquisitions (items recently added), the count of items on the shelf (checked in), and the count of items out in circulation (checked out), and shall report an aggregate total across these statuses. The system shall also report the number of holds for the selected Library and provide category breakdown counts for adult fiction and board books. The system shall provide a single consolidated Material Volume Report so users do not have to pull data manually from multiple screens, and it shall support generating reports for standard reporting periods used by libraries (for example, monthly and quarterly reports). This capability is needed by library stakeholders to produce consistent material volume reporting without manual cross-screen compilation.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is agreed core functionality for on-demand material volume visibility by Library, including the consolidated report and required subcounts/period support.

requirements.name: Material Quantity Categories
requirements.description: The system shall allow Libraries to define and use customizable categories for breaking down material quantity counts. The system shall group and report material quantity counts by reporting categories such as fiction/non-fiction and by format. The system shall show holds counts broken down per reporting category. This is needed by Libraries to configure reporting groupings and by reporting stakeholders who need consistent breakdowns for both material quantity and holds.
requirements.priority_rationale: Agreed requirements establish that customizable categories and category-based reporting of material quantities and holds are essential for acceptable reporting.

requirements.name: Material Quantity Library Scope
requirements.description: The system shall restrict item counts to Items whose Item location field equals the selected Library, so counts include only Items assigned to that Library. The system shall apply this restriction when calculating Material Quantity report results for the selected Library. This requirement ensures consistent, testable scoping for reporting so stakeholders can trust that reported quantities correspond to the intended organizational Library or branch.
requirements.priority_rationale: Correct Library scoping is essential for acceptable Material Quantity report results and for stakeholder confidence in the reporting outputs.

requirements.name: Historical Volume Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall provide date filters to produce volume counts as of any specified point in time. The system shall provide reports that show volume changes over time to support historical comparisons. This enables staff and other stakeholders to analyze how volumes evolve between dates and to retrieve point-in-time counts for comparison.
requirements.priority_rationale: Historical comparisons based on point-in-time volume counts are an agreed core reporting capability for this category.

requirements.name: Acquisition Window Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall allow reporting of Items acquired within configurable windows, such as the last 30, 60, or 90 days. The acquisition-window reporting shall support configuring the window so that the generated Report reflects the Items acquired in the selected period. This capability is needed by stakeholders to quantify how much Item volume has been added over recent time periods for acquisition review and planning.
requirements.priority_rationale: Stakeholders agreed that configurable acquisition-window reporting is required to provide timely insight into recent acquisitions.

requirements.name: Branch Capacity Overview
requirements.description: The system shall provide an interface that shows the capacity of all Library branches in the system at once. The system shall provide a high-level summary view that displays all branches and key capacity metrics together. The system shall display key capacity metrics for each branch in both the overview and branch-detail views. This capability is needed by reporting stakeholders to quickly assess branch-level capacity and compare metrics across branches.
requirements.priority_rationale: The requirement is agreed and defines the core branch capacity overview interface used for reporting at both summary and branch-detail levels.

requirements.name: Branch Capacity Drilldown
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to drill down from the high-level summary into detailed capacity information for an individual branch. This capability provides the interface to view per-branch capacity detail starting from the aggregated branch capacity summary, as agreed in PINES-015. The requirement is needed by stakeholders who want to inspect capacity at branch level without losing context from the summary view.
requirements.priority_rationale: Drilldown from summary to branch-level capacity detail is an important reporting usability function but can be worked around by alternate ways of viewing capacity details.

requirements.name: Branch Capacity Filtering
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to sort the branch list by chosen fields or metrics. The system shall allow users to filter branches by region, by library type, and by current load. The system shall allow users to group branches by system or region for the overview display. This requirement enables users to refine and organize branch capacity reporting so relevant stakeholders can analyze capacity conditions across the consortium.
requirements.priority_rationale: Filtering, sorting, and grouping are core capabilities required to make branch capacity reporting usable for stakeholder analysis.

requirements.name: Capacity Data CSV Export
requirements.description: The system shall provide an export function that allows capacity data to be exported to CSV. This requirement covers only the export capability and the CSV format for capacity data, while relying on other requirements for capacity reporting content and structure. It is needed by reporting stakeholders who require a portable, machine-readable extract of capacity data for analysis, sharing, and downstream processing.
requirements.priority_rationale: Exporting capacity data to CSV is an agreed core reporting operation needed for stakeholders to use and reuse capacity outputs outside the system.

requirements.name: Branch Capacity Trend Display
requirements.description: The system shall display trend data indicating whether a Library branch is growing or shrinking over time. This capability is required for users who need to understand branch capacity direction across time within the capacity interface.
requirements.priority_rationale: Trend direction (growing vs. shrinking) is an important reporting insight but can be worked around with separate historical capacity views in early releases.

requirements.name: Large Libraries Overview Usability
requirements.description: The system shall provide presentation options or controls to handle an overview with a large number of Libraries (e.g., 286) so the overview does not become unusable when the set of Libraries would otherwise become crowded. This capability is needed to ensure staff can effectively view a branch overview at consortium scale without the display degrading due to excessive Library count.
requirements.priority_rationale: The requirement addresses a clear usability risk for large Library counts, but it was deferred and does not replace other reporting requirements in scope.

requirements.name: Branch Capacity Color-Coding
requirements.description: The system shall support color-coding of branch capacity status using a defined mapping of green for under capacity, yellow for getting full, and red for at/over capacity. This requirement ensures that capacity status is immediately understandable to stakeholders reviewing branch capacity information in reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: Color-coded status is a usability enhancement for Branch Capacity reporting, but the system can still be acceptable without this visual mapping in an initial release.

requirements.name: Capacity Metric Configuration
requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to configure which metrics define “capacity.” The configurable metrics shall support administrator-selected definitions such as number of items versus shelf space, physical items versus a configured limit, and circulation volume versus processing capacity. This capability ensures that capacity-based reporting aligns with the consortium’s and libraries’ chosen operational meaning of capacity, which is needed by administrators configuring capacity definitions and by stakeholders interpreting capacity reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is important to enable capacity reporting to match agreed meanings, but capacity reporting can still function in a first release using a default definition of capacity.

requirements.name: Capacity Interface Mockups
requirements.description: The system shall produce initial UI mockups for the system capacity interface. Initial mockups shall be drafted for review in support of the capacity interface documentation. This requirement exists to provide stakeholders with an early visual representation of the capacity interface to guide subsequent specification and refinement.
requirements.priority_rationale: Providing initial UI mockups is important for aligning stakeholders early, but the system can be acceptable with later refinements in a first release.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Comparison Report
requirements.description: The system shall provide a Report, the Shelf Space Report, that for each genre and format enables comparison of the percentage of total circulations, the percentage of the collection (by item count), and the percentage of total shelf space. The system shall calculate the percentage of total circulations for each genre and format by summing checkouts per genre and format. The system shall calculate the percentage of the collection for each genre and format by counting items per genre and per format. The system shall calculate the percentage of total shelf space occupied by each genre and format. This requirement is needed by cataloging and reporting stakeholders to support shelf space utilization and collection/space planning comparisons.
requirements.priority_rationale: It defines the core contents of the Shelf Space Report required to perform the stated percentage comparisons for planning decisions.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Report Organizational Scope
requirements.description: The system shall produce the Shelf Space Report for individual libraries (per-branch) as well as for the whole system using an aggregated system-level view. The system shall support aggregation/grouping of report results at different organizational levels equivalent to applying GROUP BY at the appropriate level for the per-library or system-wide breakdown. This capability enables stakeholders to analyze shelf space at both the local Library level and the consolidated consortium level from the same reporting scope.
requirements.priority_rationale: Accurate shelf space reporting requires both per-Library and system-level scope as a core, agreed reporting deliverable.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Estimation Per Genre
requirements.description: The system shall estimate shelf space per genre and format using existing data. For each genre and format, the system shall use item dimension data where available to produce the shelf space estimate. When direct shelf-space measurements are not available, and item dimension data is not available for the relevant items, the system shall fall back to item count as a proxy for shelf space. The system shall provide these estimates to support shelf-space-related reporting needs for stakeholders who require capacity and distribution visibility without having direct shelf-space measurements.
requirements.priority_rationale: This estimation behavior is required to generate shelf-space estimates from available data because shelf space is not directly tracked in the database.

requirements.name: Library Shelf Space Comparison View
requirements.description: The system shall provide a comparison view that displays multiple Library Shelf Space Report breakdowns side-by-side so that outliers can be identified. The system shall display, for each Library, how its Shelf Space metrics compare to the system average. This capability supports reporting stakeholders such as branch managers who need to understand their local situation and benchmark it against the system-wide average.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is essential reporting functionality specifically required to compare Libraries’ Shelf Space metrics side-by-side and against the system average.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Date Range Filtering
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to filter the Shelf Space Report by an arbitrary date range so they can compare shelf space utilization across periods (for example, comparing Q1 versus Q2). This filtering capability shall apply to the Shelf Space Report and use the selected date range as the filter criterion. The rationale is to support staff and stakeholders who need time-based shelf space comparisons for analysis and reporting.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is an important usability enhancement for time-based comparisons, but it is not explicitly stated as mandatory for initial report acceptability.

requirements.name: Automated Shelf Space Report Generation
requirements.description: The system shall automate generation of the Report so staff do not need to pull reports manually and create spreadsheets. This requirement addresses the current workflow where staff manually pull reports and build spreadsheets, which is described as tedious. The automated generation capability is needed by staff to reduce manual effort and improve reporting efficiency for Shelf Space reporting.
requirements.priority_rationale: Automating Shelf Space Report generation eliminates the agreed core pain point of tedious manual spreadsheet creation, making the system acceptable to stakeholders.

requirements.name: Batch Item Transfer Utility
requirements.description: The system shall provide a utility to perform a Transfer of batches of Items between Libraries. The system shall also support transferring batches of Items to other designated destination types, such as mobile library and outreach collections. This utility is needed by cataloging staff because batches of Items frequently must be relocated between organizational Libraries and special units. These operations enable administrative and operational handling of Item routing without changing bibliographic structures as part of this requirement.
requirements.priority_rationale: Stakeholders agreed the batch transfer utility is important for routine inter-Library movement, but the provided sources do not establish it as mandatory for system acceptability in the first release.

requirements.name: Transfer Candidate Querying
requirements.description: The system shall provide query capability to locate candidate materials for Transfer. The system shall support identifying candidate materials for Transfer using selection criteria such as collection section and last circulation date (for example, all Items in a specified section that have not circulated within a defined time period). The capability is provided to enable staff utilities that support administrative Transfer workflows by finding the set of candidate Items eligible for Transfer. This requirement is supported by an agreed query-for-candidate capability and is complemented by proposed criteria to narrow candidates for transfer.
requirements.priority_rationale: Without candidate material querying, staff cannot identify which Items are eligible for Transfer, making the Transfer workflow incomplete.

requirements.name: Saved Reusable Transfer Queries
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to save queries for repeated use so staff can re-run commonly used item transfer queries. The system shall support reusing saved queries on a regular basis, such as monthly, to support recurring transfer workflows (for example, moving all Items in a specified genre that have not circulated in a defined time period). The system shall provide this capability within the item transfer utility. This enables administrative cataloging/transfer workflow efficiency for staff who perform the same transfer operations repeatedly.
requirements.priority_rationale: Recurring transfer workflows depend on reusing saved query definitions frequently, but the core transfer capability can still function without scheduled re-running in an initial release.

requirements.name: Shared Saved Query Templates
requirements.description: The system shall allow saved queries to be shared among users as templates. This capability shall treat shared saved queries as reusable templates that other users can use for reporting. The system shall support sharing and saving query templates to enable reuse of report query criteria across users. This requirement is needed by users to efficiently create and standardize reporting queries without rebuilding them each time.
requirements.priority_rationale: Sharing saved query templates improves reporting efficiency and consistency, but the system remains usable if sharing is deferred to a later release.

requirements.name: Manual Selection of Transfer Results
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to manually select individual titles from query results when performing a Transfer. The system shall also allow users to select a subset of query results so that only selected candidates are transferred. This selection capability shall support targeted transfers or actions by enabling users to include only the titles that they choose from the results set. This requirement is needed by cataloging and administrative users performing item transfers who must control which titles are included in a given Transfer.
requirements.priority_rationale: Selection of specific Transfer candidates from query results is an essential operation for controlled, targeted transfers and is agreed by multiple sources.

requirements.name: Batch Transfer Location Updates
requirements.description: The system shall perform batch updates to the Item location field for Item records when executing a Transfer. It shall support selecting one or more Item records and changing their Item location field to a new destination Library or other designated destination. The system shall provide an administrative capability to change records for Items to move them to a new location destination in bulk. This requirement is needed by cataloging and administrative staff to efficiently complete Transfers without updating Items individually.
requirements.priority_rationale: Batch capability to update the Item location field for selected Items is an explicitly agreed core operation for completing Transfers.

requirements.name: Printable Transfer Pull Lists
requirements.description: The system shall generate printable pull lists of items to be moved as part of a Transfer. The system shall provide mechanisms to move items by updating the Item location field to a new destination and by generating the corresponding pull lists. This requirement is needed by staff responsible for Transfer fulfillment because it supports retrieving the correct Items for movement and producing a print-ready list for use in operations.
requirements.priority_rationale: A Transfer pull list is essential to complete the item movement workflow and is explicitly agreed for the system.

requirements.name: Printable Transit Label Generation
requirements.description: The system shall generate printable transit labels, including barcodes, for items being transferred. Labels shall be produced for each item involved in a Transfer to support physical handling during transit. This capability is required by staff performing Transfers who need an unambiguous, scannable identifier for items moving between Libraries or other designated destinations. This requirement clarifies an administrative utility within the Library Automation System boundary for Transfer operations rather than day-to-day cataloging work.
requirements.priority_rationale: Without printable, barcode-based transit labels, staff cannot reliably identify items during Transfer logistics.

requirements.name: Automatic Transfer Reversion
requirements.description: The system shall include an auto-revert mechanism implemented as a scheduled task that checks transferred items and reverts them based on configured criteria. The system shall support automatic reversion of transferred items after a configurable number of days (revert after X days). The system shall be able to revert items back to their original location after the configured period, such as when a mobile library returns to base. An administrative function shall be available to revert items back to their original location. Stakeholders need this capability to ensure transferred items return automatically and administratively to their prior item location field destinations when the configured transfer period ends.
requirements.priority_rationale: Automatic, configurable reversion of transferred items is important operationally and reduces manual handling, but it can be mitigated by manual reversion for an initial release.

requirements.name: Event-Based Transfer Reversion Rules
requirements.description: The system shall support event-based reversion rules for Transfers that automatically revert an Item when item status changes to "returned". The system shall also support event-based rules for other item status changes, including automatically reverting an Item if its status changes to "sold" at the book sale. The system shall further support configurable event-based rules related to checkouts at the destination so that checkout can be used as a condition to keep or to revert Items. These capabilities are needed by stakeholders who manage Transfer outcomes to ensure Items are correctly reverted based on real-time status and checkout events at the destination.
requirements.priority_rationale: Event-based reversion behavior is core to maintaining correct Transfer outcomes and is explicitly required by agreed sources.

requirements.name: Role-Based Transfer Permission Control
requirements.description: The system shall restrict access to the transfer utility using role-based access control by limiting transfer capabilities to specified roles. The transfer capability shall be available only to roles such as managers, administrators, and transfer coordinators, and not to every staff member. This requirement ensures that only authorized staff can initiate transfers that change an Item’s holding between libraries. Stakeholders such as library administrators and security reviewers need this control to prevent unauthorized or unintended cross-library transfers.
requirements.priority_rationale: Limiting transfer utility access by role is essential to maintain security and prevent unauthorized transfers between libraries.

requirements.name: Transfer change confirmation preview
requirements.description: The system shall display a preview summary showing the count of affected Items and the source and destination Libraries before performing Transfer changes. The system shall require an authenticated User to confirm the preview before the system applies any Transfer changes. The confirmation requirement shall prevent the system from executing the Transfer changes based solely on a user’s initial request. This requirement is needed by staff and administrative Users to reduce the risk of unintended Transfers by reviewing the scope (source/destination and number of Items) prior to commitment.
requirements.priority_rationale: An agreed confirmation step is required to ensure Users review the Transfer scope before changes are executed.

requirements.name: Undo Transfer Operation
requirements.description: The system shall provide an undo function to reverse a Transfer operation when it is performed in error. This undo capability shall allow staff users to correct an incorrect transfer initiated via the transfer workflow without requiring manual re-entry of the original destination. The requirement is needed to reduce operational mistakes and recover quickly from user errors, as highlighted by the concern that an operator may click the wrong button. It applies to Transfer of an Item between a source Library and a designated destination as defined by the system’s Transfer concept.
requirements.priority_rationale: Undoing mistaken transfers is an essential safeguard for correct cataloging maintenance operations and is explicitly agreed as a requirement.

requirements.name: Transfer Delay User Notifications
requirements.description: The system shall send alerts to designated authenticated Users if an Item Transfer is delayed or encounters issues. Alerts shall be based on transfer status conditions indicating delay or problems, as requested by users who want to be notified when such issues occur. This capability supports operational awareness and timely resolution of transfer problems for staff who manage transfers.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is an agreed requirement for timely transfer issue awareness, but it is not described as a mandatory regulatory or security constraint.

requirements.name: Item Transfer History Tracking
requirements.description: The system shall track and present transfer history for an Item, including the number of times the Item has been transferred (for example, “transferred 5 times in the past year”). This transfer history shall be available to staff for reviewing how an Item has changed destination over time. The capability is required because stakeholders need transparency into transfer activity at the Item level to support operational review and auditing of Transfers.
requirements.priority_rationale: Transfer history at the Item level is an explicitly agreed requirement needed for transparency and operational auditing of Transfers.

requirements.name: Transfer Action Audit Logging
requirements.description: The system shall log all Transfer actions for audit purposes. This logging requirement applies to every Transfer that changes an Item from one Library or other designated destination to another. The audit logs are needed by Security and Access stakeholders to provide traceability of staff or administrative actions involving Item movement.
requirements.priority_rationale: Audit logging of Transfer actions is essential for security accountability and satisfies the explicitly agreed audit requirement.

requirements.name: Large Batch Transfer Updates
requirements.description: The system shall process batch updates efficiently for very large catalogs by applying updates in smaller batches to avoid locking the database. The system shall perform batch updates of the item location field using transaction safety so that partial updates cannot result in inconsistent state. This requirement supports the stakeholders who need reliable Transfer processing at consortium scale and database integrity during large catalog updates.
requirements.priority_rationale: Efficient, transaction-safe batch processing is important for large-catalog Transfer operations, but the system may remain usable with less optimized batching in an initial release.

requirements.name: Temporary Event Item Transfers
requirements.description: The system shall support transferring items to a temporary destination for a specific event or program and reverting those items to their prior destinations after the event. This capability shall apply to items within the system’s item-record data and shall treat the event or program as the driver for the temporary transfer and the subsequent reversion. The rationale is to allow participating libraries to support event-specific item routing while ensuring that collections return to their normal organization without manual reprocessing after the event, benefiting cataloging staff and event program administrators.
requirements.priority_rationale: This functionality is agreed and is core to enabling event-driven temporary routing with automatic restoration after the event.

requirements.name: Transfer Destination Types
requirements.description: The system shall allow a staff User to select a destination location type when creating a Transfer. The selectable destination location types shall include mobile library units, outreach programs, and just-in-time warehouses. This selection is used to define the intended destination category for the Transfer being created. Stakeholders need this capability to support transfers to operational delivery models such as mobile units and outreach programs, and to a just-in-time warehouse workflow.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is an agreed, practical feature for creating Transfers to common delivery destinations, but it is not strictly required for initial system usability if an alternative workflow exists.

requirements.name: Reuse Existing Report Query Tool
requirements.description: The system shall reuse the existing report query tool for candidate selection where feasible. This applies to using the query builder for candidate selection by leveraging the existing report query tool capabilities rather than introducing a separate querying mechanism. The intent is to reduce duplication of query-building functionality while still supporting candidate selection needs within reporting. Stakeholders who maintain the reporting query tooling and depend on consistent query behavior for candidate selection need this to improve reuse and implementation efficiency.
requirements.priority_rationale: Reusing the existing report query tool is an important implementation efficiency and consistency goal, but it is explicitly conditional on feasibility and can be worked around with a separate approach if needed.

requirements.name: Missing and Damaged Item Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall provide missing and damaged item Reports broken down per Library. The system shall include counts of missing and damaged Items in the Report to support auditing. The system shall include Items with status values 'missing' or 'lost' (or equivalent) in the missing/damaged Report. This capability is needed by stakeholders to generate the requested missing/damaged item visibility per Library and to show how many Items went missing or were damaged for auditing purposes.
requirements.priority_rationale: Stakeholders agreed the system must generate missing and damaged Reports per Library with auditing counts and include Items in 'missing' or 'lost' status.

requirements.name: Missing Report Filtering Controls
requirements.description: The system shall allow missing/damaged item reports to be filtered by date ranges, including predefined examples such as last 30 days and last quarter. The system shall include item condition notes in missing/damaged item reports, such as “water damage” or “vandalism”. The system shall allow missing/damaged item reports to be grouped or filtered by shelf location to identify problematic shelves for potential relocation decisions. This requirement is needed by operations and cataloging stakeholders to analyze missing and damaged item patterns accurately and take appropriate actions.
requirements.priority_rationale: These filtering and note capabilities are important for meaningful missing/damaged reporting but are not explicitly stated as mandatory for an initial release.

requirements.name: Aged In-Transit Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall generate a list of items that have been in-transit for more than X days, where X is configurable. The in-transit threshold X shall default to 7 days unless reconfigured. The system shall produce the in-transit report per Library Automation System branch and for the entire system, and it shall merge transit-to and transit-from records into a single in-transit report. The system shall generate periodic reports of items that have been in-transit for more than X days.
requirements.priority_rationale: This capability is agreed and covers the core reporting behavior, including threshold, branch/system scope, merged transit directions, and periodic generation needed by reporting stakeholders.

requirements.name: Sort In-Transit Reports by Due Date
requirements.description: The system shall allow the in-transit report to be sorted by due date so front-line staff can address the oldest items first. This sorting capability shall enable staff to prioritize in-transit items based on their due dates when reviewing the in-transit report. The rationale is to support operational workflow for front-line staff who need to chase the oldest items first.
requirements.priority_rationale: Front-line staff depend on due-date ordering of the in-transit report to prioritize urgent in-transit items, and the requirement is agreed.

requirements.name: Branch-Grouped Reports
requirements.description: The system shall allow reports to be grouped by Library branch. This grouping shall support generating report results based on queried or aggregated system data such that the grouping dimension corresponds to Library branch. This capability is needed by stakeholders who require branch-level organization of reporting outputs for analysis and comparison.
requirements.priority_rationale: Branch grouping is an agreed reporting capability, but it can be useful without being strictly required for an initial release.

requirements.name: Missing Item Trend Analysis
requirements.description: The system shall provide trending information, such as counts over time, to support collection management decisions related to missing or damaged items. The system shall use the missing/damaged data to enable collection management stakeholders to observe changes over time and make decisions accordingly. This capability ensures that stakeholders can analyze trends rather than relying only on static reporting for missing/damaged items.
requirements.priority_rationale: Trending supports collection management decisions, but it is not explicitly listed as a mandatory reporting dependency in the provided material.

requirements.name: Separate missing/damaged and in-transit reports
requirements.description: The system shall ensure its project documentation records the missing/damaged report and the in-transit report as two separate requirements. This documentation distinction shall be maintained so that each report requirement is tracked independently while still being understood as related. This requirement supports stakeholders’ review and traceability of report-specific behavior for the documentation process agreed in the project conversations.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is agreed that the report requirements must be tracked separately in project documentation to support correct documentation and traceability.

requirements.name: In-Transit Detection Logic
requirements.description: The system shall identify in-transit Items by checking the transit table for records where the arrival date is null and the departure date is more than X days ago. The requirement is intended to be a testable detection rule that flags in-transit records based on these transit-table date fields. This enables operating-environment logic needed for downstream handling of Items that have departed but have not yet arrived, supporting operations stakeholders who require reliable in-transit identification.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is an important detection behavior for correct operational handling, but it is derived from a questioned proposal and needs alignment with the separate topic of status and transit data availability.

requirements.name: Purge Candidate Identification Utility
requirements.description: The system shall provide a utility and reports to identify Item records to purge based on customizable criteria. The system shall support purging criteria based on Item status, including missing, discard/weed, and damaged. The system shall support purging criteria based on time-in-status (age), including being in a status for X months or X years, and shall support criteria based on activity using last circulated X days, months, or years ago. The system shall allow Library staff to configure numeric threshold values (e.g., X months/years and X days) used by these purging criteria so that the utility and reports can consistently select matching Item records. This requirement is needed by Library staff to review and validate which Item records will be purged before downstream purge actions are performed.
requirements.priority_rationale: The agreed utility and reports for identifying Item records to purge using configurable status, time, and activity criteria are required to enable purge candidate selection.

requirements.name: Combined Purge Criteria
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to combine multiple purging criteria to identify purge candidates using logical operators such as AND and OR. Users shall be able to specify more than one criterion as part of a single purge-candidate identification request. This capability is needed by cataloging staff to flexibly target which Items qualify for purging based on multiple conditions. It supports administrative purge workflows that require compound selection logic rather than single-criterion filtering.
requirements.priority_rationale: Combining criteria is important for accurate purge targeting, but it is not explicitly agreed as mandatory for initial system acceptability.

requirements.name: Item Status Conversion Report
requirements.description: The system shall provide a Report that assists staff in converting Items from one status to another in batch. The Report shall support batch conversion of item statuses by allowing a staff-configured set of Items to be converted from a source status to a destination status. The system shall enable batch use cases such as changing 100 Items from “missing” to “discard/weed.” This capability is needed by cataloging staff to perform efficient administrative item maintenance when multiple Items require status updates, subject to the project’s system boundary for approved administrative utilities.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is an agreed, high-value staff utility for batch item maintenance, but the system can remain usable without it via manual status updates in early releases.

requirements.name: Batch Item Status Changes
requirements.description: The system shall provide a bulk operation that changes the status of many selected Items at once, such as changing 100 Items from one status (e.g., "missing") to another status (e.g., "discard/weed"). The system shall apply the status change to the set of selected Items in a single operation rather than requiring individual updates per Item. This requirement is needed by cataloging staff to efficiently maintain Item status during administrative workflows where large numbers of Items must be updated consistently. It also supports the efficient management of Item records at scale within the system boundary for approved administrative utilities and catalog maintenance functions.
requirements.priority_rationale: Batch status conversion is an essential cataloging/administrative utility explicitly agreed by stakeholders to efficiently update many Items in a single operation.

requirements.name: Last-Copy Identification Report
requirements.description: The system shall generate a last-copy Report that, for each Item, determines whether it is the only copy within a specified scope and flags the Item as a last copy when true. The Report shall support both a per-Library view identifying items that are the only copy within a specified Library and a system-level view identifying items that are the only copy within the entire Library system or consortium. The Report shall enable cataloging workflows by singling out the library system’s last copies to assist catalogers who need to edit external records. This capability is needed by cataloging stakeholders to identify when an Item has become the sole remaining copy within the relevant scope for subsequent catalog maintenance actions.
requirements.priority_rationale: Last-copy identification is essential for cataloging and administrative maintenance workflows because the Report is explicitly treated as critical and requires accurate per-scope flagging of Items.

requirements.name: Delete Volume Records with Items
requirements.description: The system shall provide a quick method to delete Volume record entries together with their associated Item records, including support for deleting Volume record entries that have no Item records attached. The method shall support bulk deletion of such Volume record entries and their associated Item records. This utility is needed by cataloging staff for efficient item-maintenance and cleanup workflows. Clarification for the system boundary: this requirement is limited to explicitly approved administrative utilities for maintenance and purge-like operations, not day-to-day ILS cataloging.
requirements.priority_rationale: Stakeholders agreed on the need for a quick deletion utility for Volume records and associated Item records, but the scope includes bulk and no-items cases that were only proposed rather than agreed.

requirements.name: Delete Orphan Bibliographic Records
requirements.description: The system shall provide a utility to identify and delete bibliographic records that have no item records attached. The system shall generate periodic reports of bibliographic records with no item records attached and shall generate report listings of bibliographic records with no volumes attached. The system shall include a canned report for bibliographic records with no volumes attached, and shall provide a quick method to find and delete bibliographic records that have no attached item records. These capabilities support cataloging staff in cleaning up orphaned bibliographic records more efficiently by enabling both identification for review and deletion of records that have no associated Item records.
requirements.priority_rationale: The agreed requirement for an orphan-record deletion utility is essential to meet the core catalog cleanup need and make the system acceptable to stakeholders.

requirements.name: Read-Only Purge Candidate Reports
requirements.description: The system shall present purge candidate listings as read-only reports, with no immediate destructive action available from the report view. The listings shall be generated as a Report that identifies candidates for purging while preventing any destructive operation initiated directly from that view. This constraint ensures staff can review purge candidates safely prior to any approved destructive processing performed through other system functions. It is needed by staff performing catalog maintenance workflows who require a non-destructive review mechanism and by administrators who require clear separation between review and action.
requirements.priority_rationale: Reading purge candidates in a non-destructive, read-only Report is essential to safe catalog maintenance and prevents unintended deletions from the listing view.

requirements.name: Confirm Purge Deletions
requirements.description: The system shall require a separate confirmation step before performing any actual deletion of items or records identified for purge. This confirmation step shall be completed prior to initiating the deletion operation, so that purge deletions cannot be executed as an immediate consequence of selection or identification. This requirement is needed to reduce the risk of unintended data loss and to provide an explicit safeguard for staff users performing administrative purge actions.
requirements.priority_rationale: A separate confirmation step is an agreed security control that helps prevent accidental purge deletions, making it essential for acceptable administrative operations.

requirements.name: Purge audit trail logging
requirements.description: The system shall maintain an audit trail of all purge-related actions, recording who performed the purge, what was purged, and when the purge occurred. This audit trail shall capture the purge actions so stakeholders can track purge accountability and timing for security and compliance needs.
requirements.priority_rationale: An audit trail for purge actions is essential to accountability and security monitoring and was explicitly agreed.

requirements.name: Deletion Authorization Permissions
requirements.description: The system shall restrict the ability to perform deletions to users with explicit authorization/permissions to prevent accidental mass deletion. Deletion actions shall therefore require the user to be explicitly permitted before the system allows records to be deleted. This requirement is needed to make the system safe against unintended data loss and to protect stakeholders’ cataloged and administered holdings from accidental purge behavior.
requirements.priority_rationale: Restricting deletions to explicitly authorized users is essential security and safety control to prevent accidental mass deletion.

requirements.name: Scheduled Purging Utility
requirements.description: The system shall be able to schedule the purging utility to run automatically on a configurable schedule (for example, annually). This capability shall allow administrators to trigger the purging process without manual execution by running it at the configured recurrence interval. The functionality is needed by stakeholders responsible for catalog maintenance to support periodic cleanup and reduce operational effort. It is also needed to ensure purging can be performed consistently according to agreed maintenance cycles.
requirements.priority_rationale: Automation of purging on a configurable schedule is useful but was only explicitly proposed and questioned in the source, with no agreed contractual requirement.

requirements.name: Deletion audit capture
requirements.description: The system shall log every successful deletion event to an audit table so deleted records are retained for later review. The system shall implement a database trigger that captures deletion events and writes them to the audit table. The system shall also log attempted deletions that were denied due to failed authorization or validation to the audit trail. This capability is needed by stakeholders responsible for security auditing, incident review, and accountability for deletion activity.
requirements.priority_rationale: Auditability of deletion actions (including denied attempts) is an agreed core security requirement essential for later review and accountability.

requirements.name: Deletion audit actor fields
requirements.description: The system shall store deletion audit records that include record_type, record_id, deleted_by, deleted_at, and a field capturing the performing user’s Library or branch. The system shall record the type of record deleted in the deletion audit entry (e.g., item, patron, bib, other). The system shall record the timestamp (deleted_at) for each deletion event in the audit table. The system shall record the identity of the user who performed each deletion (deleted_by) and the performing user’s Library or branch for that deletion event. The system shall store the identifier (record_id) of each deleted record so specific records can be referenced, supporting security auditing and accountability for stakeholders responsible for access control and audit compliance.
requirements.priority_rationale: Storing deletion audit records with actor identity, time, and affected record details is essential for security auditing and accountability.

requirements.name: Deletion Audit Report Interface
requirements.description: The system shall provide a Report interface that can query a deletion audit table and present deletion data to Users. The system shall produce Reports showing deletions per Library and per system, and it shall provide aggregation of deletion data by date range, by User, and by record type. The system shall support total deletions for configurable reporting periods such as month, quarter, and year, and it shall break down deletions by record type (e.g., Item vs Patron vs other). The system shall produce Reports listing the top Users who delete the most records to help identify anomalies, and it shall provide audit data sufficient for auditors to demonstrate that deletions occurred in accordance with retention schedules and policies. The system shall allow staff to search and inspect deletion audit entries to troubleshoot why a specific record disappeared.
requirements.priority_rationale: This capability is required to support auditing and staff troubleshooting by querying and reporting on deletions across defined dimensions and time periods.

requirements.name: Optional Deletion Reason Capture
requirements.description: The system shall optionally capture a reason or the record’s status prior to deletion, where this information is treated as a capability to evaluate usefulness. This optional capture is based on the question of “possibly why (status before deletion?)” and is not required for all deletions. The rationale is to support Security & Access stakeholders in assessing whether recording pre-deletion context is valuable for governance, investigation, or audit-related needs without imposing mandatory data capture.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is explicitly questioned as usefulness and therefore is an optional enhancement rather than a mandatory security or compliance function.

requirements.name: Patron Characteristic Grouping
requirements.description: The system shall allow queries and reports to be limited or grouped by patron age range, zip code, county of residence, home branch, patron type, and preferred language. The system shall support using these patron characteristics as criteria for both queries and aggregated Report generation. This requirement is needed by stakeholders who require Patron demographic analysis and targeted Reporting based on different patron attributes.
requirements.priority_rationale: Stakeholders agreed that Patron characteristic-based limiting and grouping is required to support the core reporting use cases.

requirements.name: Patron Report Filtering
requirements.description: The system shall support LIMIT (filter) operations on patron reports so users can restrict the returned patron set by one or more characteristics. The system shall allow multiple filters to be combined using AND and OR logic when building patron reports. This capability is required by stakeholders who need to produce targeted patron reporting results for focused analysis and decision-making.
requirements.priority_rationale: Filtering patron reports with configurable LIMIT and combined AND/OR logic is essential to generate the correct patron subset for reporting needs.

requirements.name: Patron Report Grouping
requirements.description: The system shall support GROUP BY (aggregate) operations on patron reports so users can compute and display aggregated metrics grouped by patron characteristics. The system shall enable grouping of circulation (checkout) counts by patron characteristics such as age range. The system shall also enable grouping of patron counts by patron characteristics such as home branch. This capability is needed by reporting stakeholders who require demographic- and attribute-based breakdowns within patron reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: Agreed functionality for GROUP BY patron reporting is required to produce attribute-grouped counts demanded by stakeholders.

requirements.name: Include Patron Null Values
requirements.description: The system shall include patron records with null (missing) values in report results rather than silently excluding them, and display nulls in the relevant fields. This behavior ensures that patron characteristic reporting remains accurate by preserving records where expected patron data is not present. Stakeholders who need complete patron reporting, including staff preparing analyses and users validating report outputs, require this to avoid incomplete results caused by missing data.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is essential to prevent patron records with missing field values from being dropped and to ensure report results accurately reflect the underlying data.

requirements.name: Patron Age Range Calculation
requirements.description: The system shall compute a patron's age range at query time by calculating age from the birth_date field. The system shall allow age range (age bracket) boundaries to be configured per report, such that reports can use boundaries like 0-5, 6-10, 11-15 or alternatives such as 0-6, 7-12. This requirement is needed by stakeholders who generate demographic and patron characteristic Reports and need consistent, report-specific age bracket definitions.
requirements.priority_rationale: Accurate, configurable age-range computation from birth_date is essential for patron age reporting in Reports.

requirements.name: Patron Activity History Filtering
requirements.description: The system shall allow Report generation to filter Patrons by circulation/Transaction history, including criteria such as patrons who have not checked anything out within a specified time window (for example, 6 months). The system shall support query criteria equivalent to a request such as: show all Juvenile patrons in zip code 30505 who have not checked anything out in the past 6 months. This requirement is needed by stakeholders who need Patron behavior/activity slices for Reporting and analysis of inactive or low-activity accounts.
requirements.priority_rationale: Filtering reports by circulation/Transaction inactivity is important for Patron activity analysis, but it is not explicitly stated as mandatory for initial release.

requirements.name: Patron Reporting Data Fields
requirements.description: The system shall assume that the patron table contains the fields age (birth_date), zip code, county, home branch, patron type, and preferred language for reporting purposes. This assumption enables reporting logic to query and aggregate patron characteristics consistently. Stakeholders such as operations and reporting stakeholders need this structure to ensure generated Reports reflect the intended patron attributes.
requirements.priority_rationale: The system’s patron reporting requires the specified patron table fields to be present; otherwise reporting cannot be performed correctly.

requirements.name: Patron Null Field Documentation
requirements.description: The system shall document which Patron data fields may be inconsistently populated and specify how missing values (nulls) are represented and handled in reports. The documentation shall ensure that report consumers understand the expected null behavior for fields that may not be consistently available. This supports stakeholders who need accurate interpretation of report data when Patron characteristics are incomplete.
requirements.priority_rationale: This documentation is important for correct report interpretation, but the system can function without it in an initial release.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Reporting Interval
requirements.description: The system shall generate a list of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity in the last X days, where X is configurable. The system shall allow administrators to specify X (days) to define “inactive” as a fully customizable interval. The system shall also provide common preset inactivity ranges (e.g., 30, 90, 180, and 365 days) to simplify report configuration. This capability is needed by reporting stakeholders to identify and review inactive patrons based on a configurable time window.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is an agreed reporting function but largely depends on how broader “inactive patron” reporting is delivered (scope, fields, and export are covered elsewhere).

requirements.name: Electronic Activity for Last Activity
requirements.description: The system shall treat OPAC/patron account logins as electronic activity when determining each patron’s last activity. The system shall treat online hold placements as electronic activity when determining each patron’s last activity. The system shall treat online renewals as electronic activity when determining each patron’s last activity. The system shall treat access to digital collections as electronic activity when such access is integrated and logged, and shall compute last activity by combining activity records from the relevant circulation, OPAC logins, holds, renewals, and digital access logs sources into a unified last-activity calculation per patron. The system shall determine each patron’s most recent activity by querying the transaction and related activity tables, comparing the last activity date to X days for filtering inactive patrons. This is needed by reporting stakeholders to reliably identify inactive patrons using consistent definitions of electronic activity.
requirements.priority_rationale: This requirement defines which logged behaviors count toward “last activity,” which is essential for correct inactive patron reporting.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Report Scope
requirements.description: The system shall allow the inactive-patrons list to be generated at selectable organizational levels, including System, Home Library, and County. The system shall support configuring additional organizational/grouping levels beyond the built-in ones as needed. When generating the report, the system shall aggregate and report counts of inactive patrons by branch to show which branches have the most inactive patrons. The system shall also allow filtering the inactive-patrons list to a Home Library so branch staff can receive branch-specific cleanup lists and assign tasks. This requirement is needed by reporting stakeholders to ensure inactive patron reporting can be scoped to the appropriate organizational levels and used by branch staff to drive targeted outreach and cleanup.
requirements.priority_rationale: Scoping and branch-level aggregation are important for making inactive patron reporting usable at operational levels, though the system could still be acceptable with a limited fixed scope in an initial release.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Outreach Fields
requirements.description: The system shall include each Patron's current mailing address in the inactive-patrons report for outreach purposes. The system shall identify or flag inactive patrons who have outstanding fines so they can be handled separately. The system shall allow excluding patrons marked with a “do not disturb” flag, excluding VIP patrons, excluding staff member accounts, and excluding patrons who have opted out of communications from the inactive-patrons report. These capabilities are needed by library staff to produce accurate outreach lists that respect patron preferences and internal handling rules.
requirements.priority_rationale: These fields and exclusions are required to generate an effective and compliant inactive-patrons report for outreach.

requirements.name: Inactive Report CSV Export
requirements.description: The system shall provide the inactive-patrons report in an exportable CSV format. The system shall produce exported report files in a format suitable for upload into external outreach/marketing systems, including the ability to be uploaded to an outreach system.
requirements.priority_rationale: Exporting the inactive-patrons report as CSV in an upload-ready format is explicitly agreed and required for downstream outreach/marketing use.

requirements.name: Inactive Report Background Performance
requirements.description: The system shall run the inactive-patrons query as a background job to avoid degrading interactive system performance. The system shall cache report results for the inactive-patrons report to improve performance for repeated access to the same dataset. The system shall be designed to scale to large patron databases, such as on the order of 3.5 million patrons, without unacceptable performance degradation. This requirement is needed by stakeholders responsible for operational performance and by patrons who rely on responsive interactive system behavior while inactive-report processing occurs.
requirements.priority_rationale: Background execution and caching are essential to prevent interactive performance degradation and maintain acceptable report responsiveness, while scaling expectations ensure feasibility for large datasets.

requirements.name: Scheduled Inactive Patron Report
requirements.description: The system shall support scheduling the inactive-patrons report to run periodically (for example, quarterly) without manual intervention. The system shall enable this scheduled execution so that staff can perform routine cleanup of the patron database on an ongoing basis. This requirement ensures that the inactive-patrons report can be executed reliably and consistently at the agreed cadence, meeting operational expectations expressed by stakeholders who run it quarterly.
requirements.priority_rationale: Periodic, no-manual execution for scheduled inactive-patrons reporting is important for routine database maintenance, but it can be worked around with manual runs in an initial release.

requirements.name: Outreach Use-Case Test Scenarios
requirements.description: The system shall rely on project stakeholders to provide test scenarios for outreach use cases in order to validate the inactive-patrons Report. These test scenarios shall specifically cover the conditions required to confirm that the inactive-patrons Report is generated correctly for outreach-related validation. This documentation is needed so stakeholders can perform consistent verification of inactive-patrons reporting outcomes during outreach use case testing.
requirements.priority_rationale: Stakeholders agreed that outreach test scenarios are required to validate the inactive-patrons Report outputs.

requirements.name: Consortium Scale Capacity
requirements.description: The system shall support a library consortium with at least 286 Libraries, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing/processing of over 900,000 Items per year. The system shall be capable of sustaining these volumes as an operating environment requirement for consortium operations. This requirement ensures the system’s scalability matches the agreed consortium workload and is needed by the consortium stakeholders and system planners to confirm overall feasibility.
requirements.priority_rationale: Meeting the agreed consortium scale is essential to ensure the system can operate acceptably under expected annual circulation and item processing volumes.

requirements.name: Non-Disruptive Reporting During Open Hours
requirements.description: The system shall enable searches and reports to be processed during open hours without disrupting other system functions. The system shall separate reporting operations from production operations to avoid impacting production performance. The system shall ensure searches, reports, and report processing do not disrupt or slow down the OPAC or circulation client during open hours. The system shall queue and perform long-running searches and report generation in background processing so report generation does not slow down or disrupt the circulation client. The system shall not constrain or interfere with the OPAC and shall not slow down OPAC performance when reports run. This requirement is needed by library staff and system operators to maintain service availability for patron-facing clients while reporting is executed.
requirements.priority_rationale: Disrupting OPAC or the circulation client during open hours is unacceptable to stakeholders and would undermine core library operations.

requirements.name: Supported Server Operating Systems
requirements.description: The system shall operate on a server environment running Linux or Solaris. It shall be deployable and operable on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 for the primary server environment. It shall also be deployable and operable on Solaris 10 on SPARC hardware to support the secondary/disaster recovery site. The system shall work across both Linux and Solaris platforms so that system reporting and operations are available in either environment. This constraint is needed by the system stakeholders responsible for operations and disaster recovery to ensure the system can be deployed on their existing server platforms.
requirements.priority_rationale: Stakeholders agreed the system must run on Linux and Solaris, including specific Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 and Solaris 10 SPARC environments for primary and disaster recovery.

requirements.name: Web and Windows Client Access
requirements.description: The system shall be accessible through a web browser or a Windows-compatible client. This accessibility method applies to the system’s management processes as well. This requirement ensures stakeholders can access the system using common client options for day-to-day operations and management workflows.
requirements.priority_rationale: Access through a web browser or a Windows-compatible client is agreed and is essential for stakeholders to use the system’s management functions.

requirements.name: Supported Web Browsers
requirements.description: The system shall be accessible through Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6.0 and later and Mozilla Firefox version 2.0 and later when accessed via a web browser. This constraint applies to the system’s web-browser-based access, including management process access. This requirement is needed by the system administrators and management to ensure the system functions in the browsers currently in use.
requirements.priority_rationale: Stakeholders agreed the system must support Internet Explorer 6.0+ and Mozilla Firefox 2.0+ to be acceptable for web-browser access.

requirements.name: Assistive Technology Accessibility Support
requirements.description: The system shall be accessible with screen-reading software, screen-magnification software, and other assistive technology programs. The system shall comply with Section 508 accessibility requirements. The system shall be usable with common screen readers such as JAWS and NVDA and with screen magnification software such as ZoomText, and it shall be compatible with other assistive technology programs used by staff. The system shall provide accessibility support for the report interface and ensure HTML output is compatible with different browsers and assistive technologies such as screen readers.
requirements.priority_rationale: Accessibility support and Section 508 compliance are explicitly required and agreed by stakeholders.

requirements.name: Relational Database Backend and Schema
requirements.description: The system shall use a fully relational database back-end. The system shall be compatible with PostgreSQL databases, operating against the environment’s PostgreSQL 8.3. The system shall operate against the existing normalized relational database schema and shall not require denormalized reporting schemas. The system shall avoid denormalized reporting schemas that would create synchronization issues. This constraint is needed by the system administrators and technical stakeholders to ensure the new system aligns with the existing database platform and schema maintenance practices.
requirements.priority_rationale: A fully relational, PostgreSQL-compatible design aligned to the existing normalized schema is an agreed platform constraint required for acceptance.

requirements.name: Standards-Compliant HTML Output
requirements.description: The system shall generate standards-compliant, properly structured semantic HTML for web-based components, reports, and help content. The system shall ensure its HTML validates against W3C standards for all web-based interfaces and report output. For images included in the HTML output, the system shall provide alt attributes. For interactive elements, the system shall include ARIA labels where appropriate to improve accessibility.
requirements.priority_rationale: These requirements are agreed and explicitly define standards compliance and accessibility-related HTML content needed for acceptable web, report, and help presentation.

requirements.name: Separated Dev/Test Environments
requirements.description: The system shall provide separate development, training, and production environments so developers and staff can test and practice running reports without affecting production data or operations. The system shall provide the ability to migrate reporting configuration from the development and training environments to the production environment. Reporting configuration migration shall support exporting and importing report templates and related configuration, including permission settings and saved queries. The system shall provide a development and training environment that is safe for staff experimentation without risking production data, and this configuration migration capability shall be available to support management processes. This requirement is needed by system administration and management stakeholders to support safe development and training and to enable controlled promotion of reporting configuration into production.
requirements.priority_rationale: Separate environments and configuration migration are required to safely develop and train without impacting production and to support moving reporting configuration into production.

requirements.name: Role-Based Access Control
requirements.description: The system shall implement role-based access control using security groups and/or roles to control authorization for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups. The system shall allow permission control through security groups and/or role assignments. The system shall enable administrators to change a staff member’s permissions by changing the staff member’s role assignment rather than modifying individual permissions, and it shall provide an administration interface that makes it easy to administer roles and permissions. The system shall support definable and assignable roles for staff and allow administrators to create and manage security groups and roles.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is an agreed security requirement that defines how authorization is controlled and administered across staff, workgroups, and groups.

requirements.name: OPAC Read-Only and No Patron Functions
requirements.description: The system shall not include day-to-day patron-facing functions; such functions shall remain part of the Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC) module and the circulation client. The system shall interact with the patron interface (OPAC) in a read-only manner and shall not modify OPAC data. The system shall not constrain the functionality or features of the Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC) module. The system shall not manage acquisitions or cataloging functions, and it shall read and report on ILS data instead. This boundary clarifies the operating environment responsibilities needed by consortium stakeholders to ensure the OPAC and circulation client remain authoritative for patron workflows and bibliographic maintenance, while the reporting system remains non-invasive.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is essential to establish system scope and prevent unauthorized or conflicting behavior with the OPAC and the authoritative acquisition/cataloging processes.

requirements.name: Record Data Dictionary Specifications
requirements.description: The system shall provide complete data specifications (data dictionary) for authority records, bibliographic records, order records, item records, hold/request records, and other records maintained or accessed by the Management Processes. These data specifications shall include the full set of record definitions necessary to support the Management Processes’ use of each record type. The system shall ensure the same level of completeness applies across all listed record categories. This requirement is needed by the Management Processes stakeholders to ensure consistent, unambiguous record structures for development and integration.
requirements.priority_rationale: Complete data specifications are essential for the Management Processes to correctly maintain and access all required record types.

requirements.name: Major Process Descriptions
requirements.description: The system shall include a high-level process description for bibliographic record import and export, for validation of bibliographic records against internal and external authority sources, and for standard reports. The high-level descriptions shall be thorough and cover these major processes as part of the system documentation. This requirement is needed by the system stakeholders to understand how core bibliographic workflows operate and how the system generates standard reports. It also supports developer and reviewer alignment on process behavior related to authority validation and record data exchange.
requirements.priority_rationale: Thorough documentation of major processes is important for stakeholder understanding and review, but the system can be acceptable without it in an initial release.

requirements.name: Online Hierarchical Help System
requirements.description: The system shall provide an online help system in HTML that is hierarchical and cross-linked, and that describes and illustrates all system functions. The system shall ensure the online help system is accessible and works with screen readers. The system shall include help that is integrated with the reports interface and supports navigation through the help content. The online help system shall also provide searchable content to support users in finding system functions. This requirement is needed by patrons, system administrators, and technical stakeholders to ensure complete, discoverable, and accessible documentation for using all system functions.
requirements.priority_rationale: Accessible online help that works with screen readers and covers all system functions is essential for acceptable system usability and compliance.

requirements.name: Administrator Error Feedback Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback when reports fail. The system shall allow Local and Global System Administrators to view low-level, query-specific error feedback from the front-end interface. The query-specific error feedback shall include table, field, and error type where possible. This requirement is needed by Local and Global System Administrators to diagnose report failures using both summary (high-level) and detailed (query-specific) information.
requirements.priority_rationale: Clear error reporting and administrator-level query diagnostics are essential to acceptable report troubleshooting and operation.

requirements.name: Enterprise ILS Infrastructure Assumptions
requirements.description: The system shall assume that the Management Processes are part of an enterprise-level Library Automation System and can rely on that system’s infrastructure. The system shall assume that enterprise infrastructure services are available, including redundant servers, backup systems, and network connectivity. The system shall assume the Management Processes rely on the data structures and functionality of an enterprise-level Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and Cataloging modules, and that the Management Processes are consolidated at a central location to accept input and provide services to multiple locations. The system shall assume interaction with a patron interface also known as an Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC), and that the system can interface with vendor websites via published APIs and/or automated transfer of standard-format data files such as USMARC21 and EDIFACT. These assumptions are required so stakeholders can plan the operating environment and integration dependencies for the Management Processes within the enterprise Library Automation System context.
requirements.priority_rationale: Without these enterprise and integration environment assumptions, the Management Processes cannot operate or interoperate with required infrastructure and related systems.

requirements.name: Staff Login Methods
requirements.description: The system shall support streamlined staff login methods, such as card swipe using an RFID employee badge, for ILS terminals or staff workstations, while making these streamlined methods optional (supported but not required). The system shall also support traditional individual login credentials consisting of a username and password as an available login method and as a fallback when card-reader hardware is not available. Streamlined login methods shall not bypass individual authentication; the individual’s identity must still be authenticated. The system shall function in locations that do not have card-reader hardware by not requiring card readers to operate the system, enabling staff to authenticate using the supported alternative method. This requirement is needed by staff and operations at varying branch sites to ensure convenient login without weakening authentication security.
requirements.priority_rationale: Supporting both optional streamlined login and guaranteed username/password fallback improves usability and operational continuity across sites while preserving required authentication behavior.

requirements.name: Staff Login Identity Auditing
requirements.description: The system shall track which staff member is logged in for audit purposes. This requirement ensures audit stakeholders can attribute system actions to an identifiable staff member during authenticated use, supporting security oversight and accountability.
requirements.priority_rationale: At minimum, auditability requires recording the identity of the currently logged-in staff member for security and accountability.

requirements.name: Fast Staff Login and Switching
requirements.description: The system shall reduce staff login time to minimize service slowdowns during busy periods. The system shall provide mechanisms to reduce security risks such as password sharing and unattended logged-in terminals, including faster login and switching behavior. The system shall allow quick switching between different staff users on shared public service computers so that multiple staff members can use the same terminals throughout the day, such as where 15 public service computers are used by 8 different staff members during the day. This requirement is needed by staff and operations to keep service responsive and by library management to reduce common security risks arising from hurried login and left-unattended terminals.
requirements.priority_rationale: Improving staff login speed and switching directly supports operational responsiveness and reduces identified security risks, but the system may remain usable with slower login in an initial release.

requirements.name: Report Template Creation
