requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to create report templates that are available to staff. The system shall provide a report template management capability for creating, storing, and versioning templates. The system shall also support determining and creating report templates needed for all Library units within the consortium. Created report templates shall be capable of being run as-is or modified before running. This capability is needed by administrators and reporting stakeholders to ensure staff can generate required reports using managed, reusable templates.
requirements.priority_rationale: Template creation and management are essential to enable staff reporting using templates for all Library units.

requirements.name: Report Template Run and Edit
requirements.description: The system shall allow report templates to be run as-is or be modified for individual needs, and it shall allow staff to edit canned reports for display purposes. Administrators shall be able to limit which filters and display fields in a template can be altered by staff so the system can certify dependable output. The system shall prevent staff from altering templates to display deleted items or other administrator-restricted data, and it shall prevent or warn about modifications that would compromise the intended results of a report template. The system shall centrally manage report templates to ensure consistent criteria when staff run standard reports. This is needed by administrators and staff to safely reuse templates while maintaining consistent, dependable report results.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is required to enable controlled template modification while preserving report result integrity and consistent criteria for acceptable reporting.

requirements.name: Report Template Integrity
requirements.description: The system shall ensure that changes to templates do not compromise the accuracy of results. This requirement covers integrity of results produced when report templates are changed, so that stakeholders can trust reporting outputs after template updates. It is needed by reporting stakeholders who rely on accurate results for decision-making and by developers who must maintain correctness through template evolution.
requirements.priority_rationale: Accurate report results following template changes are essential to acceptable reporting outcomes.

requirements.name: Fine-Grained Report Permission Controls
requirements.description: The system shall implement distinct, fine-grained permission levels that limit who may create, clone, modify, or run reports. The system shall allow administrators to create shared folders that permit or deny staff from running specific reports. The system shall allow administrators to permit or restrict staff from running ad hoc reports on specific sets of data using shared folders or similar constructs. The system shall make report permissions easy to administer. This requirement is needed by administrators and security stakeholders to enforce controlled access to report creation, cloning, modification, running, and ad hoc execution on defined data sets.
requirements.priority_rationale: Fine-grained report permission controls and shared-folder administration are important for secure and manageable access to reports, but a basic access model may remain usable in an initial release with workaround administration.

requirements.name: Report Query Builder Interface
requirements.description: The system shall provide a user-friendly interface for designing queries against all record types, including bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, and financial. The system shall also provide a web-based report writer interface that supports drag-and-drop field selection. The system shall support creation, storage, and execution of custom/local reports used by libraries for collection development, program tracking, and staff productivity. This capability is needed by Library staff to build and run the queries and reports required for day-to-day library operations and reporting needs.
requirements.priority_rationale: Staff require an interface to design and execute queries across all core record types, and custom/local reporting is essential for stated library use cases.

requirements.name: Report Query Field Selection
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff to select which fields to query through the query interface when defining a Report. The system shall support staff checking off or selecting specific data/fields to include in the report. The system shall expose all relevant database fields for selection in report definitions rather than limiting selection to a subset. This capability is needed by staff to configure reports based on the specific fields they require for their reporting needs.
requirements.priority_rationale: Selecting query fields is core functionality for creating usable Reports via the query interface.

requirements.name: Query Criteria Picklist Selection
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff to select values for query criteria from a picklist of possible values when building queries. This capability shall support staff in choosing among predefined criteria values rather than entering them manually. The requirement is needed by reporting stakeholders to ensure efficient and consistent query construction for report generation.
requirements.priority_rationale: Selecting query-criteria values from picklists is essential to acceptable report query building functionality for staff.

requirements.name: Dropdown Regular Expression Query
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff to select regular expressions from a dropdown in the query interface. The system shall provide regular-expression matching options that are selectable from the same dropdown. The system shall provide regular expression support for report query filters so staff can use regular expressions in filtering. This capability is needed by staff to build and refine report queries using regular expressions.
requirements.priority_rationale: Staff need regular-expression selection and matching options in report query filtering, but one proposed source indicates it is not mandatory for an initial release.

requirements.name: Query Boolean Operators
requirements.description: The system shall support Boolean operators (e.g., AND, OR, and NOT) during query construction, enabling staff to build queries beyond simple filters. The system shall provide a full range of Boolean operators for constructing queries. This capability is needed by reporting users to express more complex query logic when generating Reports and retrieving relevant data.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is an agreed feature that enables more advanced query logic for reporting, but it is not explicitly indicated as mandatory for initial system acceptability.

requirements.name: Administrative Data Access Controls
requirements.description: The system shall provide administrative controls that allow administrators to restrict staff access to database tables and to individual fields. The system shall also provide administrative controls to restrict access to the query tool. These controls shall support limiting who can view or query specific data and which staff can use querying capabilities. This requirement is needed by administrators and security stakeholders to ensure appropriate access governance for reporting and system data access.
requirements.priority_rationale: Access restriction for both database data structures and the query tool is essential to meet the system’s Security & Access goals.

requirements.name: Executive Report Templates
requirements.description: The system shall provide pre-defined Board and Executive reports for consumption by library boards and external consumers. These pre-defined board reports shall include basic statistics required by the Georgia Annual Report and similar external reporting needs. The system shall provide an Executive Reports Interface and include a compiled list of reports needed for that interface. The system shall provide pre-defined board and executive report templates to support routine executive reporting.
requirements.priority_rationale: Executive and board reporting templates and the Executive Reports Interface are required to meet mandated Georgia Annual Report statistics and to support routine executive reporting consumption.

requirements.name: Activity Metrics Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall produce Reports showing traffic and volume of use. The Reports shall include statistics for check-outs, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled. This functionality enables staff and other stakeholders to understand system usage and circulation activity at a summary level for reporting and decision-making.
requirements.priority_rationale: Activity Metrics reporting is explicitly agreed and provides core circulation-hold usage statistics needed for acceptable reporting functionality.

requirements.name: Activity Cross-Tabulation
requirements.description: The system shall allow cross-tabulation of activity statistics per terminal, branch, library system, hour, patron age range, patron type, and patron location. The system shall support generating cross-tabulated report metrics using these same dimensions: terminal, branch, system, hour, age range, patron type, and patron location. This capability enables stakeholders to analyze activity variations across multiple operational and patron characteristics for reporting and decision-making.
requirements.priority_rationale: Cross-tabulation across these dimensions is important for reporting analysis but is not explicitly indicated as mandatory by the sources beyond agreement.

requirements.name: Transaction Archive Privacy Controls
requirements.description: The system shall archive Transaction data in a manner that protects Patron privacy as defined by applicable State Law and shall comply with that State Law. The system shall archive Transaction records without retaining personally identifiable information in the transaction archive. The system shall still provide useful demographic statistics from the archived Transaction data while maintaining Patron privacy.
requirements.priority_rationale: Protecting Patron privacy under applicable State Law and prohibiting personally identifiable information in the archive are essential constraints for system acceptability.

requirements.name: Periodic Holds Reports
requirements.description: The system shall generate periodic reports that list bibliographic records with holds and that also generate periodic reports of item-level holds. Periodic reporting shall include both the bibliographic record view of holds and the item-level view of holds. This capability is needed by Library stakeholders and reporting users to routinely monitor hold activity at both the bibliographic and item granularity for operational awareness and decision-making.
requirements.priority_rationale: Recurring hold reporting is an important expected reporting function, but the system can remain acceptable in an initial release without it if an alternative manual reporting approach exists.

requirements.name: Items Without Recent Checkout
requirements.description: The system shall generate periodic Reports of items that have not been checked out in X days, where X is configurable. The reporting period shall be established by the system’s recurring report mechanism so that the items meeting the “not checked out in X days” criterion are included each time the periodic Report is generated. This requirement enables stakeholders to identify items with potentially stale circulation and support collection management decisions based on checkout recency.
requirements.priority_rationale: It provides useful recurring insight for collection and circulation monitoring, but the system can be acceptable without it in an initial release.

requirements.name: Invalid Item Type Periodic Reports
requirements.description: The system shall generate periodic reports of items that have an invalid item type. The periodic reports shall include all items whose item type is invalid. This capability is needed by stakeholders who require ongoing visibility into catalog or item classification issues to support timely review and remediation.
requirements.priority_rationale: Ongoing reporting of invalid item types is important for operational oversight, but it is not defined as mandatory by the provided source and may be deferred in favor of other reporting requirements.

requirements.name: In-Transit Holds Periodic Reports
requirements.description: The system shall generate periodic reports of in-transit items that have outstanding holds. Each generated report shall include in-transit items with outstanding holds as the report contents. This requirement is needed by staff and reporting stakeholders who require recurring visibility into items currently in transit and still subject to holds.
requirements.priority_rationale: Periodic visibility into in-transit items with outstanding holds is important for operational tracking and decision-making, but it can be deferred depending on release scope.

requirements.name: Long Call Number Periodic Report
requirements.description: The system shall generate periodic reports of items that have a long call number. The periodic reports shall include the set of items with a long call number. This requirement enables stakeholders to monitor and review items requiring attention due to their long call number classification through scheduled reporting.
requirements.priority_rationale: Periodic long call number reporting is an important reporting capability, but it is not explicitly stated as mandatory for initial system acceptability.

requirements.name: Invalid Patron Home Library Reports
requirements.description: The system shall generate periodic reports listing patrons whose home Library is invalid. Periodic reports shall include the set of patrons with an invalid home Library, based on the system’s patron data. This requirement is needed by stakeholders who require data-quality visibility and ongoing monitoring of patron home Library assignment status.
requirements.priority_rationale: Periodic invalid home Library reporting is important for data quality monitoring, but the initial release can be acceptable without it if an alternative reporting or manual remediation process exists.

requirements.name: Report Criteria Display
requirements.description: The system shall display the query selections (criteria) alongside the query results so users can see what criteria were used to generate the report. When configuring reports, the system shall present selection criteria that are clearly defined to users. The system shall include the date selection criteria and report name at the top or bottom of report results to indicate the selected date range and report name. This capability is needed by users to interpret report results and to verify the criteria used to produce them.
requirements.priority_rationale: Users must be able to view the report’s applied criteria (including date range and report name) to understand and validate generated report results.

requirements.name: Report Queue Position Visibility
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff and users to see where their Report is in the execution queue by displaying its position in the queue. The system shall display queue details for submitted Reports, including whether the Report is in the queue, how many Reports are ahead, the submission time, and the status. Queue status shall be shown using the states waiting, running, completed, and failed. This requirement ensures stakeholders can track progress and understand whether a submitted Report is still processing, needed by staff and users who submit or monitor Reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: Queue visibility with position and status is important for user confidence and operational follow-up, but the system can remain usable without it in an initial release via other monitoring approaches.

requirements.name: Attached Report Specifications
requirements.description: The system shall support the reporting definitions described in the attached report examples in Appendix A, and it shall support the fine-grained reports requirements described in the attached specification in Appendix B. These capabilities ensure the system can generate the required Report content and structure as specified by the reporting materials supplied to the project, which is needed by stakeholders responsible for reporting requirements and validation against the appendix documents.
requirements.priority_rationale: Supporting the attached reporting definitions and fine-grained reports requirements is important for meeting agreed reporting expectations, but the provided sources are only proposed rather than agreed or explicitly mandatory.

requirements.name: Patron Behavior and Usage Analytics
requirements.description: The system shall produce statistics and analytics that can be used to understand and predict patron behavior and material usage. The system shall compute, for a particular Item, how quickly that Item is returned on average. The system shall compute, for a particular Item, the likelihood that the Item will be renewed. The system shall compute what percent of check-outs at a Library are renewals. This capability is needed by stakeholders who want analytics (for example renewal likelihood and percent renewals) to support understanding and prediction of patron behavior and how materials are used.
requirements.priority_rationale: The need for patron behavior analytics is stated but only as proposed examples of analytics, without indication of mandatory scope or calculations beyond illustrative metrics.

requirements.name: Demographic Statistics Reports
requirements.description: The system shall produce aggregated demographic statistics derived from archived transactions, including transactions by geographical region and transactions by age ranges. The system shall provide useful aggregated demographic statistics for demographic analysis reports that support program planning. The system shall preserve individual privacy while generating the aggregated demographic statistics. Stakeholders needing program planning and reporting analytics require these demographic views to understand transaction patterns across regions and age ranges without exposing individual data.
requirements.priority_rationale: This capability is explicitly agreed and required to generate demographic statistics from archived transactions while preserving individual privacy to support program planning.

requirements.name: Demographic Report De-identification
requirements.description: The system shall anonymize demographic data used for statistics by deleting information that could be used to identify a patron. The system shall anonymize demographic statistics produced in demographic reports to ensure that no personally identifiable information is exposed. This anonymization requirement applies to the demographic data used as the basis for statistical outputs, ensuring that identifying elements are removed prior to report generation. Stakeholders including security and privacy reviewers need this control to reduce the risk of patron re-identification from demographic reporting.
requirements.priority_rationale: Because demographic statistics must not expose personally identifiable information and identifying elements must be deleted, this privacy/anonymization control is essential for acceptable system security and compliance.

requirements.name: Uncataloged Inventory Tracking
requirements.description: The system shall provide the ability to control inventory of uncataloged material, such as paperback books and children’s board books. The system shall allow tracking uncataloged material as inventory even when individual catalog records (volume record) are not present. This capability supports handling large shipments that arrive without individual catalog records, enabling staff to track and manage those items as Item inventory under the system’s boundary for administrative utilities rather than replacing day-to-day ILS cataloging.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is important for practical cataloging workflows involving shipments without catalog records, but it is not explicitly indicated as a legal/security critical requirement in the provided candidates.

requirements.name: Quick Distribution for Uncataloged Materials
requirements.description: The system shall support quick distribution workflows for uncataloged material so incoming materials can be processed fast. The system shall provide low-effort processing operations that minimize per-item branch labor, including for large shipments, to enable efficient handling with limited staff time. This capability applies to uncataloged material tracked or circulated without an individual catalog record. The requirement is needed by library staff to reduce time spent per item and to accelerate processing of uncataloged shipments at branches, particularly during high-volume arrivals.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is important for efficient branch operations and fast processing of incoming uncataloged material, but it is not evidenced as mandatory for initial system acceptability.

requirements.name: Uncataloged Material Usage Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall provide the ability to identify how uncataloged material is being used and shall record how uncataloged materials are being used so that usage can be analyzed. This supports reporting needs for stakeholders who require visibility into uncataloged material usage patterns in order to evaluate and analyze usage over time.
requirements.priority_rationale: Understanding and analyzing uncataloged material usage is important for reporting and assessment, but it is not defined as mandatory in the provided sources.

requirements.name: Uncataloged Circulation Statistics
requirements.description: The system shall count transactions for uncataloged material and include those transactions in circulation statistics and reports. The system shall generate a Non-Cat Count circulation report. The system shall generate a NonCat In House Use Count by month report. The system shall include a canned report for Non-Cataloged Count. This requirement is needed by stakeholders responsible for circulation statistics and reporting to ensure uncataloged material usage is reflected in standard and canned reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: Counting and reporting uncataloged material transactions is important for complete circulation statistics, but it can be deferred if initial releases focus on cataloged-only reporting.

requirements.name: Transaction History Retention
requirements.description: The system shall maintain transaction history for X days, where X is configurable. The system shall retain monthly aggregate and annual aggregate information indefinitely. The system shall enforce data retention policies required for audits by retaining specified data for seven years where mandated. The system shall retain archived transaction data for the retention period required by State Law, configurable to the legally required number of years. This requirement is needed by security and compliance stakeholders to ensure audit readiness and legal retention of transaction records and aggregates.
requirements.priority_rationale: Retention of transaction history and legally/audit-mandated archives is required to meet security and regulatory compliance obligations.

requirements.name: Transaction Dimension Grouping
requirements.description: The system shall allow transactions to be grouped by hour, terminal, branch, and system for backroom statistics. The system shall support transaction grouping by hour to facilitate identification of busy periods. This requirement ensures reporting stakeholders can analyze circulation or financial Transaction patterns by the specified dimensions for backroom statistics and operational workload insights.
requirements.priority_rationale: The requested grouping dimensions are important for backroom statistics and busy-period identification, but they are not described as legally or security mandatory.

requirements.name: Transaction Type Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall record and report transaction types including check-ins, check-outs, fines collected, and patron registrations. The system shall include these transactions in statistics and queries. The system shall allow queries of all transactions or filtering results by specific transaction type. This requirement is needed by stakeholders who require transaction type visibility for reporting and analysis of circulation and financial events.
requirements.priority_rationale: Transaction type breakdown and type-filtered querying are important for meaningful reporting, but they can be deferred without blocking initial overall transaction statistics reporting.

requirements.name: Check-In Type Counts
requirements.description: The system shall count all types of check-in individually and cumulatively, including book-drop, and provide counts by terminal and by user or self-service. The system shall treat each check-in type (including book-drop and terminal and user/self-service channels) as separate counts while also maintaining cumulative totals across all check-in types. This enables reporting stakeholders to understand check-in patterns and overall volumes needed for operational and management oversight.
requirements.priority_rationale: Counting check-in types individually and cumulatively is a core reporting need explicitly required by the proposed requirement.

requirements.name: Check-Out and Renewal Counts
requirements.description: The system shall count all types of check-out individually and cumulatively, including staff check-out, self check-out, staff renewal, self check-out renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal. The system shall provide counts that separately distinguish each check-out and renewal type while also producing an overall cumulative count across all listed types. This requirement is needed by stakeholders who rely on consistent circulation and renewal reporting breakdowns for analysis and decision-making.
requirements.priority_rationale: Accurate individual and cumulative counts across check-out and renewal types are important for reporting, but the system can still be usable with a less granular release approach.

requirements.name: Hold Placement Method Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall count all hold requests and record how each hold was placed. The recorded placement method options shall be at a staff desk, at a public computer inside the Library, or remotely. The system shall include the method of placement when generating holds count reports so that holds can be reported by placement method. This requirement enables stakeholders to analyze and survey how patrons place holds, supporting reporting needs identified in the early drafts and survey results.
requirements.priority_rationale: Capturing the placement method for every hold request is essential to produce the intended holds reporting breakdown by staff desk, public computer, and remote placement.

requirements.name: Transaction Report Scopes
requirements.description: The system shall generate transactions reports for holds placed, holds filled, and check-outs at the following aggregation scopes: per patron, per Library, per selected group of Libraries, per system, and per county. The system shall display, within patron-scoped transaction reports, the number of check-outs and the number of placed holds. The system shall support transaction report dimensions that match these scopes while reflecting the relevant transaction types (holds placed, holds filled, and check-outs). The rationale is to enable reporting stakeholders to analyze circulation and hold activity by individual patrons and by varying organizational and geographic groupings, supporting both operational review and survey-driven reporting needs.
requirements.priority_rationale: Correct transaction report scope and granularity are essential so stakeholders can generate the required circulation and hold reports at patron, Library, system, and county levels.

requirements.name: Hold Type Subtotaling
requirements.description: The system shall subtotal holds by type in transaction reports. The hold types shall include active, frozen, and frozen-until holds. This enables stakeholders to view transaction reporting with hold type breakdowns, supporting clearer hold management reporting needs.
requirements.priority_rationale: This provides useful reporting detail but is not explicitly required beyond existing transaction and reporting capabilities.

requirements.name: Item Value Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall generate a report of the value of items based on data in item records for the entire collection or for a selected portion of the collection. The system shall use the item record purchase price field as the source of item value and be able to query and aggregate that field to support the report. The system shall allow value reports to be filtered by item status and by collection attributes such as format (e.g., DVDs in a children’s collection) to enable staff to obtain value for relevant subsets. This capability is needed by library staff to produce value reporting across an entire collection or targeted segments for decision-making and financial awareness.
requirements.priority_rationale: This provides the core “value of items” reporting functionality required by agreed reporting expectations and depends on using the purchase price field for value aggregation.

requirements.name: Accounting and Audit Compliance
requirements.description: The system shall ensure that all Report generation and all data archiving comply with standard accounting practice and with state, county, and municipal auditing requirements. This compliance shall apply to the content and storage of the archived data used to support reporting and audit needs. The rationale is to meet financial oversight obligations and expectations of organizations and oversight stakeholders responsible for accounting and audits.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is an essential compliance constraint covering auditing and accounting requirements for reports and archived data.

requirements.name: Financial Transaction Record Association
requirements.description: The system shall attach fines, charges, waivers, and ecommerce transactions to patron records and item records in the database. The system shall support joining the financial data attached to patron records and item records when generating financial reports. The system shall make reportable records for action_circulation, action_hold, and money (fines/payments) available for reporting and linking to patrons and items. This requirement is needed by staff and reporting stakeholders to ensure financial report generation can accurately relate financial transactions to the relevant patron and item.
requirements.priority_rationale: Accurate association and joinability of financial data across patron and item records is essential for generating financial reports.

requirements.name: Fines Waiver and Payment Tracking
requirements.description: The system shall track fines waived and payments made per Library and shall track and present payments collected at each Library so each Library can see payments collected at its location. The system shall support tracking fines waived and payments made per library/location for budgeting and reporting purposes. This requirement is needed by financial and reporting stakeholders to produce end-of-month reports and to enable budgeting and per-branch visibility of payments collected.
requirements.priority_rationale: The agreed sources indicate it is important for budgeting and end-of-month reporting with per-branch visibility, but a workaround may exist for an initial release.

requirements.name: Authorized Financial Record Editing
requirements.description: The system shall allow financial information to be updated by authorized staff. Access to update financial information shall be restricted to users with appropriate authorization based on Role-based access control. The system shall record that an authorized update occurred as part of the financial record editing process, enabling Security & Access monitoring of changes. This requirement is needed by authorized staff to maintain accurate financial information while ensuring that only permitted staff can alter sensitive financial data in the Library Automation System.
requirements.priority_rationale: Editing financial information is essential for system operation and must be controlled to protect security and integrity of financial records.

requirements.name: Patron Account Balance Queries
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff to query patron accounts whose balances are greater than a specified threshold amount (greater than X dollars). The threshold amount shall be provided as part of the query so that only patrons meeting the “greater than X” condition are returned. This capability supports financial reporting needs by enabling staff to identify patrons with balances above an amount of interest for subsequent reporting or review.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is an agreed reporting function that staff need for balance-focused analysis, but it can be delivered alongside broader patron balance reporting workflows.

requirements.name: Patron Balance Report Scopes
requirements.description: The system shall provide financial reports of patron account balances for each individual Patron, by home Library, and for the entire system. The reports shall support the three aggregation scopes: by patron account, by home Library, and system-wide totals. This requirement is needed by stakeholders who require visibility into patron financial standing at the patron level, across a patron’s home Library, and at consortium-wide scale.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is a core reporting capability for financial oversight, agreed by stakeholders, though it is not explicitly stated as the only reporting scope within the overall reporting set.

requirements.name: Fines and Charges Time-Breakdown
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports of fines and charges accrued per configurable time period. The system shall support specified time periods such as last 12 months, year-to-date, and last month. The system shall break down accrued fines and charges in the report by type of charge, including overdue fines, damaged item charges, and lost item charges. This capability is needed by stakeholders who require periodic financial reporting with clear time scoping and category-based breakdowns.
requirements.priority_rationale: Financial stakeholders need time-scoped, type-based fine and charge reporting, but the system may be acceptable without it in an initial release if an interim reporting approach exists.

requirements.name: Waived Fine Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports showing fines waived per configurable time period and per branch. The report scope shall be at the Library level as defined by the participating branch or library within the consortium. This capability allows stakeholders to monitor waived fines consistently across branches over time, supporting financial reporting needs identified in the early drafts and confirmed by stakeholders.
requirements.priority_rationale: Reporting on fines waived by time period and branch/library is an agreed financial reporting requirement necessary for acceptable system behavior.

requirements.name: Payment Reporting by Method
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports of payments made per time period and broken down by payment method types. Payment method types shall include cash, credit card, check, and similar methods, and shall be reported using payment methods such as staff desk, self-check station, and OPAC. The reporting shall aggregate payment totals according to the selected time period and the chosen payment method breakdown so stakeholders can analyze payment composition and channels. This requirement is needed by finance and operations stakeholders to understand payment intake patterns for reporting and reconciliation purposes.
requirements.priority_rationale: Finance stakeholders require payment reporting broken down by both time period and payment method types for acceptable financial reporting.

requirements.name: Patron Payment Ledger Reconciliation
requirements.description: The system shall maintain a ledger of patron payments and record which charges each payment was applied to in order to facilitate reconciliation. The system shall maintain this as an audit ledger of patron payments so finance staff can trace every payment back to the specific charge it was applied to. This capability ensures finance-related reconciliation workflows are supported by providing auditable payment-to-charge associations needed by finance staff and stakeholders responsible for financial reporting integrity.
requirements.priority_rationale: Accurate and auditable reconciliation between patron payments and the specific charges they apply to is essential for finance staff to perform financial reconciliation and traceability.

requirements.name: Circulation Count Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall generate a Check in Count circulation report. The system shall generate a Checkout Count circulation report that includes checkouts only, and a Renewals Count report. The system shall generate a circulation report that includes total circulation combining checkouts, renewals, and Uncataloged material circulation, and shall generate a Total Circulation Count report by merging category and Uncataloged material circulation data. The system shall retrieve total circulation including checkouts, renewals, and Uncataloged material and display a breakdown showing those circulation types, and shall include canned reports for Checkout Count and Renewals Count.
requirements.priority_rationale: These circulation-count reports and canned templates are important reporting outputs requested by stakeholders, but the system can be usable without them in an initial release.

requirements.name: Overdue Item Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall generate reports listing items overdue by a configurable number of days. The system shall support overdue reporting views including a daily view, a shelf reading view, and a patron contact information view, and it shall include a canned report format for “Items Overdue by X Days.” The system shall generate an Overdue Materials report for items more than a configurable number of days overdue, and it shall generate reports for items marked longoverdue by the system, including a “List of Long Overdue” report. The system shall allow running reports for pre-overdue, overdue, and holds notices sent. This capability is needed by library staff to identify overdue items, manage collections, and perform patron outreach using patron contact information.
requirements.priority_rationale: Overdue reporting is an expected operational reporting capability, but it can be delivered in a first release with a narrower set of the proposed overdue and view variations.

requirements.name: Circulation Breakdown Reports
requirements.description: The system shall generate circulation count reports broken down by circulation modifier and by category fields (Cat1, Cat2 such as Adult, YA, Juv). The system shall also generate circulation count reports grouped by Dewey call number ranges, and by shelving location. The system shall further generate circulation count reports by MARC fields, and by circulation location broken down by patron county and patron home library. The system shall provide a circulation count report broken down by patron age demographic. These reports are needed by stakeholders who require circulation breakdown analysis across item and patron dimensions to support reporting and management decisions.
requirements.priority_rationale: While multiple breakdown report variants are proposed, none are marked as agreed or mandatory and availability is noted as partially available or not available for several breakdown dimensions.

requirements.name: Item Activity Count and Lists
requirements.description: The system shall generate Reports for item activity including an Items Added Count report, an Items Deleted Count report, an Items Edited Count report, and an Items Count report for total item counts. The system shall also generate item list Reports including a List of Items Added report, a report listing Items currently checked out, a List of Items by Creation Date Range report, and Claims Returned report. The system shall support weeding and threshold-based item list Reports by generating a report listing items with a total use count greater than a specified threshold and a report listing items with a total use count less than a specified threshold for weeding purposes, and it shall generate a weeding report including date of last circulation and number of circulations for items. The system shall provide item use count Reporting by generating item total use counts and use counts broken down by usage date range (for example, fiscal year use count and monthly use count).
requirements.priority_rationale: This set of canned item activity, checkout, and weeding Reports is important for reporting workflows, but no evidence indicates it is mandatory for the first release.

requirements.name: Deleted Last Copy Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall generate a Last Copy Report listing items that were the last copy owned by the Library and that were deleted. The system shall provide this list of deleted last-copy items so it can be used to update external catalogs such as WorldCat. The system shall allow running a report on deleted items that were the last copy in the facility. This capability is needed by library staff and catalog maintenance stakeholders to audit deletions and support external catalog synchronization.
requirements.priority_rationale: It supports a specific operational need (external catalog updates and last-copy deletion reporting) but is not stated as mandatory for core system acceptability.

requirements.name: Item and Bibliographic Field Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall generate a Report listing Items whose bibliographic_record contains a specified string in a specified field. The system shall pull MARC record fields and present selected fields on a single row of Report data. The system shall make bibliographic_record fields available to reporting, including id, fingerprint, edition, ISBN, publisher_name, publication_date, and physical_description. The system shall make item fields available to reporting, including id, barcode, copy_number, item location field, status, call_number, purchase_date, shelving_location, and reserve_id, where item location field is the technical item-record field identifying an Item’s assigned Library or other destination. This capability is needed by staff users to support flexible reporting and analysis across bibliographic_record and Item metadata.
requirements.priority_rationale: Core reporting requires filtering by bibliographic content and presenting bibliographic_record and Item fields in a row-based Report for staff users.

requirements.name: Collection Age Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall generate an Age of collection Report by call number and by shelving location. The system shall also provide an Age of collection Report by call number when requested. This capability supports stakeholders who need to analyze how old the collection is for reporting and decision-making purposes.
requirements.priority_rationale: Age of collection reporting is important for collection analysis, but only by call number is explicitly supported in one candidate, making it non-essential for an initial release.

requirements.name: Bibliographic Record Activity Reports
requirements.description: The system shall generate a Bib Records Count report and a Bib Records Edited Count report. The system shall generate a report of Bib Records added by user by library with counts using the Bib Records Added by user by library Count metric. The system shall include a canned report for Bib Records Count. The system shall include a Bib Records Edited Count report, noting it was indicated as not available. The system shall provide a report of Bib Records added by user by library with counts, noting it was indicated as not available.
requirements.priority_rationale: These bib record activity reporting metrics are important for staff visibility into bibliographic record creation and edit activity, but the sources indicate some candidates were not available yet.

requirements.name: Patron Count Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall generate a Patron Count report of total patrons. The system shall include a canned report for total Patron Count. The system shall generate a Patron Added Count by Month report. The system shall generate a New Patron Count report of patrons added the previous month by demographic category. The system shall generate Patron Count reports by age demographic, county, home library, profile group, and by survey answer, including a List of patrons by survey answer. The system shall generate a Patron Count report by county, city, and zip code, and provide Patron Count reports by county, city, and zip code. These reporting capabilities are needed by stakeholders to summarize patron growth and composition across multiple patron characteristics and locations for analysis and oversight.
requirements.priority_rationale: These reports are important for understanding patron totals and distribution but are largely additive reporting features proposed without explicit agreed mandatory status.

requirements.name: Survey Response Counts by Week
requirements.description: The system shall generate Voter Survey Responses count reports by week, including a county breakdown for the Voter Survey Responses by county by week reports. The system shall also generate Voter Registration survey responses count reports by week. The system shall provide reporting for Voter Survey Responses. The reporting shall support filtering by survey name, where the system resolves survey names to survey identifiers internally rather than requiring entry of a survey id.
requirements.priority_rationale: The reports and survey-name filtering are important for providing usable voter survey response reporting, but they were not explicitly stated as mandatory in the source set.

requirements.name: Patron Expiration and Status Reports
requirements.description: The system shall generate reports that list patrons by expiration date. The system shall also generate a report listing patrons who are BARRED. In addition, the system shall generate a report listing staff accounts with the date of last password change and the account expiration. The system shall generate a report listing patrons with specific wording in their notes, and the system shall provide a report of Staff Accounts including date of last password change. This set of reports supports staff needs for account lifecycle monitoring, security-related oversight, and identification of patrons requiring attention based on status or notes.
requirements.priority_rationale: These reports are important for routine patron and staff account management and security oversight, but they are not explicitly stated as mandatory and can be delivered in an incremental release.

requirements.name: Hold Management Reports
requirements.description: The system shall generate a Report of Items Sent for Holds and a Report of Items Received for Holds. The system shall generate a Holds Purchase Alert Report and an Unfilled Holds Report. The system shall generate a Stale Holds Report for holds sitting on the hold shelf waiting for pickup for too long, and it shall generate an Annual number of holds placed Report. These Reports are needed by stakeholders to manage and monitor the end-to-end hold lifecycle and identify issues such as unfilled and stale holds, as well as track holds placed over time.
requirements.priority_rationale: The candidate Reports are important for operational hold management but are not stated as mandatory or agreed in the provided sources (all are proposed).

requirements.name: Cataloged In-House Use Count Report
requirements.description: The system shall generate a Cataloged In House Use Count report. The report shall present a count of in-house use for cataloged items as a generated Report. This capability is needed by library staff to obtain summarized reporting on cataloged item in-house use.
requirements.priority_rationale: This report is an important in-house usage summary, but it is not explicitly stated as mandatory by the provided source.

requirements.name: In-Transit Direction Reports
requirements.description: The system shall generate in-transit item reports to support delivery coordination between Library branches. The system shall generate a report listing items in transit that includes both the sending Library and the destination Library. The system shall also generate an “Items In Transit to Destination Library” report. The system shall also generate an “Items In Transit by Sending Library” report. This capability is needed by delivery coordination stakeholders to monitor and manage item flow directionally between branches.
requirements.priority_rationale: Directional in-transit reporting is important for delivery coordination, but it is not explicitly stated as mandatory in the provided sources.

requirements.name: Interlibrary Loan Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall generate IntraPINES Loans reports for all systems and additionally by system and by facility. The generated reports shall support the scopes “all facilities” and “by facility” in addition to “all systems” and “by system.” This capability provides staff with the necessary Interlibrary Loan Reporting views to understand loan activity at both consortium-wide and more granular organizational levels.
requirements.priority_rationale: Generating IntraPINES Loans reports by system and facility is useful for analysis, but it is only listed as a proposed capability with no explicit mandatory commitment.

requirements.name: Financial Transaction Reports
requirements.description: The system shall generate a Bills currently Owed by Patrons report. The system shall generate reports of Detailed Payments Received. The system shall generate a Detailed Forgive, Work, and Goods Payments Received report and a Detailed Voids report. The system shall generate Aged Debt reports and shall include canned report templates for Bills Currently Owed by Patrons, Detailed Payments Received, and Aged Debt. This capability is needed by stakeholders who require financial transaction visibility for reporting on patron balances and payment-related events.
requirements.priority_rationale: These reporting outputs are important for financial oversight of patrons and transactions, but the sources are marked proposed and do not indicate mandatory legal or security requirements.

requirements.name: Reporting Interface Types
requirements.description: The system shall provide three reporting interfaces: canned reports, noncanned/on-demand reports, and open template reporting. Each interface shall support selecting attributes for filtering and display, so that users can generate reports based on the chosen attributes. This requirement establishes the available ways to create and run reports that other reporting requirements rely on. It is needed by staff who produce and review reports and by stakeholders defining the reporting capabilities and user experience.
requirements.priority_rationale: Providing the three distinct reporting interface types is an important expected capability for the reporting feature set, but it can be phased if a workaround exists.

requirements.name: Canned Report Templates
requirements.description: The system shall include a set of pre-written canned report templates delivered with the product. The system shall allow adding more canned reports based on role-based access control permission levels. This requirement ensures that staff can immediately use standardized reporting templates and that authorized stakeholders can expand the template set safely according to their permissions.
requirements.priority_rationale: Providing shipped canned report templates and permission-controlled extensibility is important for practical reporting adoption, though it can be partially worked around without adding new templates in an initial release.

requirements.name: Relative Date Range Canned Reports
requirements.description: The system shall allow canned reports to run for relative date ranges including yesterday, last week, last month, and last year. The system shall execute the report using data corresponding to the selected relative date range, such that the report reflects the appropriate time period at execution. This capability is needed by stakeholders who require recurring reporting without manually selecting fixed date criteria each time.
requirements.priority_rationale: Relative date ranges for canned reports are important for practical scheduled reporting, but the system could still be acceptable using fixed-date selection in an initial release.

requirements.name: Batch Report Execution
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to select multiple canned reports to run at the same time. The system shall allow users to check off multiple canned reports from a list for simultaneous execution. The system shall display the results of concurrently executed selected reports within a single document. This enables stakeholders to efficiently produce and review multiple Report outputs together without requiring separate executions.
requirements.priority_rationale: Batching multiple canned reports into one document is important for efficient reporting workflows, but the system can remain usable without it in an initial release.

requirements.name: On-Demand Report Editing
requirements.description: The system shall provide On Demand reports that are preset but allow editing of selection criteria and display options. The system shall enable these preset On Demand reports to be run on demand. This capability ensures stakeholders can generate customized reports when needed without requiring a separate predefined report for every variation, supporting staff reporting workflows that need timely query adjustments and presentation changes.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is important for enabling flexible, timely report generation from preset templates, but it may be deferred if a more limited preset-only reporting capability is acceptable for an initial release.

requirements.name: Open Template Query Fields
requirements.description: The system shall provide an Open Template reporting interface that exposes all attributes associated with circulation, patrons, items, bills, and bibs for filtering and for choosing display attributes. These same attributes available for filtering shall also be available for selection of fields to display in the generated Report. This capability enables staff to configure report query criteria and presentations without being limited to a predefined set of fields. It is needed by staff who create and run flexible Reporting to support different analysis and presentation needs using consistent attribute definitions.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is an important capability for flexible Reporting configuration and usability, but it can be initially supported through narrower, predefined templates in early releases if needed.

requirements.name: Canned Report Title Descriptions
requirements.description: The system shall display a pop-up description when the user hovers over each title of a canned report or template in the reporting interface. The system shall provide a quick access interface with pop-up descriptions for reports. The system shall provide hover tooltips for report titles in the interface. This requirement is needed by staff users to quickly understand what each canned report or template title represents while browsing and selecting reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: Hover/pop-up title descriptions improve usability for report selection and comprehension, but the system remains usable without them in an initial release.

requirements.name: Scheduled Report Execution Options
requirements.description: The system shall allow scheduling reports to run either immediately using a Run ASAP option or automatically on a configurable recurring schedule. The configurable recurring schedule options shall include hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly intervals, and users shall be able to select the applicable scheduling option(s). The system shall also support scheduling reports to run at specified times and shall allow users to cancel a scheduled or running report. This capability is needed by stakeholders who require reliable, automated report generation and timely execution without manual initiation.
requirements.priority_rationale: Recurring and time-based report scheduling is important for automated reporting workflows, but the system can be acceptable with limited scheduling capabilities in an initial release.

requirements.name: Multi-format Report Export
requirements.description: The system shall export report results in Excel, HTML, and CSV formats. It shall support exporting report results in CSV format, HTML for web display, and Excel format suitable for pivot tables. The exported report output formats shall include CSV, HTML, and Excel to accommodate different stakeholder reporting workflows. This requirement is needed by business users and staff to obtain report results in the formats required for analysis and web viewing.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is an agreed requirement ensuring core report export deliverables in Excel, HTML, and CSV for stakeholder use.

requirements.name: Email Report Delivery
requirements.description: The system shall allow entering email addresses for report delivery and support an address book of regularly used addresses. The system shall support delivering scheduled or on-demand reports via email. Email delivery shall enable sending one or more generated reports to one or more recipients.
requirements.priority_rationale: Email delivery of reports is explicitly required to send generated reports to recipients, and existing sources indicate it is a core expectation rather than a deferred enhancement.

requirements.name: Recurring Report Selection Editing
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to edit recurring reports by adding or removing report selections and editing the recipient email addresses. This capability shall cover modifications to both the set of selected reports within a recurring report and the email addresses to which the recurring report is delivered. The feature is needed by stakeholders who manage recurring report content and distribution to keep report delivery accurate over time.
requirements.priority_rationale: Editing recurring report selections and recipient email addresses is an important usability requirement to maintain correct recurring reporting, but it is not necessarily essential for the system’s initial acceptability.

requirements.name: Comparative Report Columns
requirements.description: The system shall support report output formatting that produces comparative columns for time periods and related percent differences. The system shall allow a report result set to include columns for last month's circs and previous month's circ, and a column for the percent difference. The system shall also support comparative month and year columns such as the previous year's month and percent difference between the last month and last year's month. This capability is needed by stakeholders to analyze circulation trends across comparable periods using consistent report column structures.
requirements.priority_rationale: Comparative columns are important for circulation trend analysis, but the system can still be acceptable without them in an initial release.

requirements.name: Canned Report Display Options Editing
requirements.description: The system shall allow editing of canned report display options. This requirement is needed because stakeholders require staff to modify how a canned Report is displayed without being limited to a fixed set of presentation settings.
requirements.priority_rationale: Enabling edits to canned report display options is important for maintainability and usability, but the system may still be acceptable using non-editable options in an initial release.

requirements.name: Report Queue Prioritization
requirements.description: The system shall allow reports to be assigned priorities so that higher-priority reports are advanced ahead of lower-priority reports in the processing queue. The system shall also support prioritizing certain types of reports so they are moved to the top of the queue ahead of resource-consuming reports. The system shall allow administrators or authorized roles to assign or change the priority of reports so important reports can jump the queue. This capability is needed by executive stakeholders and operational roles (e.g., directors and staff) to ensure important reports are processed first and to provide the desired queue management behavior.
requirements.priority_rationale: Prioritized processing of reports is agreed as important for workflow and board-level versus ad-hoc needs, but it is not stated as legally or security mandatory.

requirements.name: Report Filter Text Upload
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to upload a text file containing filter input, including lists of barcodes and TCNs, for use as filter criteria in reports. The system shall use the uploaded text file contents to filter report results according to the provided barcode or TCN values. This requirement enables users to supply external lists for report filtering, which supports reporting stakeholders who need flexible report criteria without manual entry.
requirements.priority_rationale: Uploading text-file filter criteria is an important reporting convenience expected by stakeholders, but the system can still be acceptable without it in an initial release.

requirements.name: Pivot-Ready Report Output
requirements.description: The system shall support pivot table output for report results. The system shall provide pivot table style output for report results. The system shall be able to produce report output suitable for pivot table analysis, including pivot-ready export output. This capability is needed by stakeholders who want to analyze generated report results using pivot table techniques.
requirements.priority_rationale: Pivot-ready output is important for downstream analysis workflows, but the system can still produce reports without this feature in an initial release.

requirements.name: Validated Report Output
requirements.description: The system shall provide tested and proven Report output, ensuring validated output formats and correctness. The system shall ensure data exported to Excel and other tabular formats does not contain unintended duplicate rows. This requirement is needed so stakeholders can trust that generated reports use correct formats and produce accurate, reliable tabular exports.
requirements.priority_rationale: Validated, correct report output with de-duplicated tabular exports is essential for stakeholders to rely on reporting results.

requirements.name: Cancel Scheduled or Running Reports
requirements.description: The system shall allow users or administrators to cancel a scheduled report or a running report. When a report is in progress, the system shall check for cancellation signals during report processing so running jobs can be stopped promptly. This capability covers report jobs that are already scheduled to run or are currently running, and ensures cancellation can take effect during processing rather than only between processing phases. The requirement is needed by stakeholders who operate reporting workflows and require the ability to halt report execution when it is no longer desired.
requirements.priority_rationale: Cancelling scheduled and running report execution with prompt stoppage is essential operational functionality agreed by the technical subcommittee.

requirements.name: Include Null and Blank Values
requirements.description: The system shall include all nulls and blank fields in report results for any report, rather than omitting them. The system shall not implicitly filter out null or blank fields due to filtering or display settings. When null and blank fields are requested, the system shall include them in the results explicitly. This requirement is needed by stakeholders who rely on complete and accurate reporting outputs for downstream analysis and validation.
requirements.priority_rationale: Including null and blank fields in report results is essential for report correctness and prevents misleading omissions.

requirements.name: Real-Time Reporting Support
requirements.description: The system shall provide real-time reporting capabilities by generating reports based on up-to-the-minute transactional data. The system shall support reporting on live changes as required, including reports that reflect current overdue items as of today. The system shall provide real-time or near-real-time reporting capability adequate for monitoring busy periods. This requirement ensures staff can monitor critical operational conditions using the most current transactional data, particularly for overdue items and high-demand times.
requirements.priority_rationale: Stakeholders agreed that some reporting needs to be real-time (e.g., what is overdue today) and surveys indicate it is needed for busy-period monitoring.

requirements.name: Historical Reporting Warehouse
requirements.description: The system shall provide historical reporting using a reporting warehouse so that data can be acquired for a given date or date range. The system shall support historical reporting in the form of time-based reports and historical reports. The system shall provide historical snapshot reporting that shows data as it appeared on a specific past date, regardless of subsequent shelving location changes. These capabilities are needed by stakeholders who require answers to questions about what the data looked like on a specific past date or for a specified time period.
requirements.priority_rationale: Stakeholders agreed on historical reporting needs, but the reporting warehouse and snapshot-specific requirement were proposed rather than explicitly confirmed as mandatory for the first release.

requirements.name: MARC Field Consolidated Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall allow selection of specific MARC fields for reports and shall present the selected MARC field values consolidated per record rather than spread across multiple rows. This enables staff to pull targeted bibliographic information without fragmentation in the report layout. It is needed by reporting stakeholders who require MARC field reporting that is readable and aligns with their expectations for consolidated per-record presentation.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is important to meet core usability needs for MARC field reporting, but it is not stated as mandatory for an acceptable first release.

requirements.name: Transaction Audit Query
requirements.description: The system shall allow running a Report of Transactions that occurred on a specified date and time, filtered by either a specified workstation or a specified staff member. The report criteria shall support selecting the occurrence date and time and selecting the relevant workstation or staff member to scope the returned Transactions. This requirement supports audit and investigations by enabling staff to retrieve the exact subset of recorded circulation or financial events for a targeted time and actor.
requirements.priority_rationale: Audit reporting for Transactions scoped by date/time and workstation or staff member is essential to support investigation and verification needs.

requirements.name: Immediate Financial Data Reflection
requirements.description: The system shall reflect updates to financial information immediately when staff record a payment, including payments made at the front desk, so the financial data is current for reporting and reconciliation. This requirement ensures that each recorded Transaction is available for downstream Report generation and reconciliation without delay, minimizing the risk of discrepancies. It is needed by library staff responsible for accurate financial reporting and reconciliation and by stakeholders who require up-to-date financial data for operational integrity.
requirements.priority_rationale: Immediate reflection of recorded payments is essential to keep financial data current for reporting and reconciliation, as agreed by stakeholders.

requirements.name: Report Template Cloning
requirements.description: The system shall provide a clone feature that creates a new report/template based on an existing one without altering the original. This clone operation shall take an existing template and use it as the source for creating the new template instance. The new report/template must be produced as a separate artifact so that subsequent use does not change the original template. This capability is needed by reporting stakeholders to reuse existing report/template configurations while preserving template integrity.
requirements.priority_rationale: Template cloning is agreed and important for efficient report authoring and reuse, but it does not appear as a blocking requirement for initial reporting functionality.

requirements.name: Automatic Report Permissions Update
requirements.description: The system shall support role-based administration so that when a user’s role is changed (for example, from Staff to Manager), the user’s report permissions are updated automatically according to the assigned role. This requirement ensures that role changes immediately take effect for authorization to access Reports, reducing the risk of incorrect or outdated permissions and supporting the security needs of administrators and security stakeholders.
requirements.priority_rationale: Automatic permission updates on role change are essential to correct role-based access control for report access and therefore are required for system security.

requirements.name: Configuration Migration Import/Export
requirements.description: The system shall provide export and import of report templates to support migration between environments. The system shall provide export and import of permission settings to support migration between environments, including the permission settings associated with the exported configuration. The system shall provide export and import of saved queries to support migration between environments, so that saved query definitions can be moved along with templates and permissions. This capability is needed by stakeholders to enable consistent configuration transfer across environments during migration activities.
requirements.priority_rationale: Stakeholders agreed that migration requires export/import of report templates, permission settings, and saved queries as core operating-environment functionality.

requirements.name: User-Saved Report Definitions
requirements.description: The system shall allow Users to save report definitions and reuse them for later report runs. The system shall also allow Users to save queries and reuse them for repeated report runs. This requirement enables Users to avoid reconfiguring report definitions and queries when generating the same reports multiple times, improving staff efficiency and reporting consistency for stakeholders who run repeated reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: Saving and reusing report definitions and queries is an important usability expectation for repeated reporting, but it is not explicitly indicated as mandatory in the provided sources.

requirements.name: Report Writer Filtering and Sorting
requirements.description: The system shall provide basic filtering and sorting capabilities in the report writer interface. The system shall allow filtering reports by all relevant fields and not restrict filtering to a limited subset. These capabilities ensure stakeholders can narrow report results accurately across the applicable dataset and control the order of returned information in the report writer interface.
requirements.priority_rationale: Filtering across relevant fields with basic sorting is important for practical report authoring, but the system can potentially be usable with limited capabilities in an initial release.

requirements.name: Background Report Processing
requirements.description: The system shall provide background processing for long-running reports so they do not block interactive operations. The system shall support queuing and background processing of complex reports so they can run asynchronously without impacting interactive use. This capability is needed by system administrators to ensure report execution does not degrade interactive performance for users.
requirements.priority_rationale: Blocking interactive operations during long-running or complex reports is explicitly identified as requiring background queuing and processing to meet stakeholder expectations.

requirements.name: Reporting Replica Offload
requirements.description: The system shall run reporting workload using a separate reporting database or a read-only reporting replica to offload reporting queries from the production database. This approach ensures reporting workload does not execute against the production database. The system shall be able to use read-only reporting replicas for this purpose. This requirement is needed to support non-disruptive separation of reporting from production operations for stakeholders operating and maintaining production services.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is an important agreed mechanism to achieve separation of reporting from production, though the evidence indicates the broader separation requirement exists elsewhere and this specific database/replica approach may be an implementation option.

requirements.name: Evergreen Version and Reporting Assumptions
requirements.description: The system shall assume the analysis and requirements apply to the Evergreen codebase version 1.4.0.4 and the PINES production usage patterns. The system shall further assume the current Evergreen reporting implementation runs queries against the production database and that no separate reporting database replica exists. This assumption ensures that requirements behavior and expected data access patterns are grounded in the production environment used by stakeholders at PINES.
requirements.priority_rationale: The assumption is important to align requirements with the PINES production baseline, but it is not inherently a core functional/security obligation for system acceptance.

requirements.name: Record Relationship Joins
requirements.description: The system shall support joins between record types following key relationships, including bibliographic_record to item via asset.copy and item to action.circulation via circulation transactions. These joins shall enable report generation that combines related data across the specified record types using the defined key relationships. This capability is needed by staff responsible for Reporting to create reports that derive insights from related bibliographic, item, and circulation data without requiring manual correlation outside the system.
requirements.priority_rationale: Join support between related record types is important for producing meaningful cross-entity reports, but the system may still be usable with limited or manual correlation in an initial release.

requirements.name: Secondary Disaster Recovery Deployment
requirements.description: The system shall be deployable to the secondary disaster recovery site for reporting operations. The system’s reporting operations shall run successfully on the secondary disaster recovery site environment, which is specified as Solaris 10 on SPARC hardware. This constraint supports continuity of reporting in the event of a primary site failure and is required by the system administrators responsible for disaster recovery and reporting operations.
requirements.priority_rationale: Deployment to the secondary disaster recovery site is agreed as essential for resilient reporting operations.

requirements.name: SRS Basis and Documentation Approach
requirements.description: The system shall have its requirements specification based on the King County Library System/Galecia Group draft, adapted for PINES. The system shall be documented in an SRS that specifies optimal Reports functionality for a future Evergreen release and includes a list of requirements. The SRS shall be written for both library managers and staff and for software project managers and developers, balancing readability for non-technical readers with specificity for developers. This basis and documentation approach is needed to ensure consistent requirements traceability and to support both operational stakeholders and delivery teams.
requirements.priority_rationale: These documentation commitments are essential to define and align the system requirements and to communicate them to both library and software delivery stakeholders.

requirements.name: Working Group Report Testing Gate
requirements.description: The system shall filter all new Report development through the Reports Working Group, which shall act as the reports testing group. This filtering shall ensure that any new Reports produced by the system development process are reviewed by the Reports Working Group prior to acceptance. The requirement is needed by the Reports Working Group and system stakeholders to establish a consistent testing and governance gate for all new Reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: An agreed governance constraint is required to ensure all new Report development is reviewed by the designated testing group.

requirements.name: Management Process Scope
requirements.description: The system shall focus on Management Processes, providing reports and analysis tools used by library managers, administrators, and staff to support planning, evaluation, and oversight. The system shall specify only those requirements that directly or indirectly relate to management activities, excluding requirements that do not have such a relationship. This constraint ensures the operating environment and functional scope remain aligned with stakeholder expectations for management-focused capabilities and clearer requirement traceability for managers and administrators.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is an agreed scope constraint that defines what the system will cover for management process reporting and analysis.

requirements.name: Collection Usage Analysis Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide Report and analysis tools to analyze the library collection and its use by patrons.
