These tools shall support generating reports based on queried or aggregated system data to support collection-usage analysis. This requirement enables stakeholders to understand how the library collection is being used by patrons and to make informed reporting decisions based on those analyses.
requirements.priority_rationale: Without collection usage Report and analysis tools, the system cannot deliver the core reporting capability agreed for this requirement area.

requirements.name: Branch Capacity and Collection Distribution Analysis
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports and analysis tools to analyze branch capacity and determine the optimal distribution of the collection. The analysis shall support evaluating how capacity constraints relate to recommended collection distribution across Libraries. This capability is needed by stakeholders to make data-driven decisions about branch planning and collection allocation based on branch capacity and collection distribution findings.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is an agreed reporting requirement, but it is not directly restated with measurable acceptance metrics in the provided candidates beyond the existence of the reports and analysis tools.

requirements.name: Patron Demographic Analysis
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports and analysis tools to analyze patron demographics and patron interests. Reports and analysis shall be based on aggregated system data related to patrons and present results in support of demographic and interest insights. This capability is needed by stakeholders who require understanding of patron characteristics to inform service decisions and reporting needs.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is an agreed reporting capability that supports important patron insights, but the requirement is broad relative to other more specific reporting items in this category.

requirements.name: Staff Productivity and Workflow Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide Report and analysis tools to analyze staff productivity and workflow. The tools shall support analyzing staff productivity and workflow by generating reports from queried and aggregated system data. This capability is needed by staff and administrators to understand how work processes are performing and to support operational review and improvement.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is an agreed reporting capability for analyzing staff productivity and workflow, but it is not specified with measurable acceptance criteria in the provided material.

requirements.name: Financial Transaction Verification Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports and tools to track and verify financial transactions. The reports shall support verification of financial transactions as recorded in the system, enabling staff or administrators to review transaction details needed for tracking and verification purposes. The tools shall enable tracking and verification activities for financial transactions so that stakeholders can audit and confirm transaction records. This requirement is needed by stakeholders who manage financial records and require reporting support to verify recorded financial events.
requirements.priority_rationale: This capability is agreed as necessary for financial transaction oversight, but it is not further constrained here with measurable verification/audit actions beyond tracking and verifying.

requirements.name: User Class Role-Based Permissions
requirements.description: The system shall support the defined user classes—Patron, Staff, Local System Administrator, Library Manager, Library Director, and Global System Administrator—using role-based access and capabilities. The system shall provide a Global System Administrator role with full system access. The system shall provide a Local System Administrator role with branch-level reporting and configuration privileges. The system shall provide a Library Manager role that can run approved reports and perform limited template modification. The system shall provide a Staff role that can run reports within assigned permissions. This requirement is needed by security and system stakeholders to ensure consistent authorization across interacting user classes and to delegate reporting, configuration, and administrative capabilities appropriately.
requirements.priority_rationale: Defining role-based access for the required user classes is essential to meet the security and authorization needs of the system.

requirements.name: Local System Administrator Configuration
requirements.description: The system shall allow Local System Administrators to configure the system locally for their organizational units. This requirement ensures that administrators responsible for specific organizational units can manage system configuration without relying on Global Administration, addressing the operational needs of Local System Administrators and the organizational governance expectations of participating units.
requirements.priority_rationale: Local unit configuration by Local System Administrators is explicitly agreed and is essential for meeting the consortium’s access and administration model.

requirements.name: Global System Administrator Administration
requirements.description: The system shall allow the Global System Administrator to implement software changes and configurations and to generate statistical reports for PINES as a whole. This capability is needed by administrators who manage consortium-wide operations and require both system configuration control and consolidated statistical reporting across PINES.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is an agreed, security-relevant administrative function but is limited to a specific administrator role and does not replace other access control and reporting permissions requirements elsewhere in the category.

requirements.name: Functional-Focused Initial Specification
requirements.description: The system shall establish initial specifications that emphasize functional requirements. Detailed user interface specifications shall be deferred to later iterative specification rather than included in the initial specification set. This approach ensures the stakeholders first align on what the system must do before committing to UI details, supporting efficient progression of requirements work.
requirements.priority_rationale: The agreed meeting decision explicitly mandates an initial focus on functional requirements with UI details deferred.

requirements.name: Iterative UI Prototype Specification
requirements.description: The system shall specify its user interface and data structures using an iterative, prototype-oriented methodology. The system shall be developed in a highly collaborative and iterative environment that provides multiple opportunities for end-user review of prototypes. This requirement ensures that stakeholder feedback can be incorporated early and throughout development, benefiting end-users and the team responsible for user interface and data structure definition.
requirements.priority_rationale: Collaborative iterative prototyping is important for aligning the interface and underlying data structures with end-user needs, but it is not strictly necessary for an initial acceptable release.

requirements.name: Assumed Library Terminology Knowledge
requirements.description: The system shall assume that readers have a general understanding of Library services and processes and therefore need not define common Library terminology within the SRS. This assumption applies to the SRS readers’ need for explanations of terminology rather than to any operational behavior of the system. The purpose of this assumption is to reduce unnecessary documentation detail while maintaining shared baseline understanding. Stakeholders who author and review the SRS need this assumption to streamline terminology coverage.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is a documentation scope assumption intended to streamline the SRS, but the system would remain acceptable if common terminology were defined instead.

requirements.name: Architecture Review Meetings
requirements.description: The system’s requirements process shall include architecture review meetings and a technical subcommittee. The requirements process shall schedule and hold at least one technical subcommittee meeting in late June to discuss architectural constraints. The requirements process shall schedule and conduct a follow-up review meeting on July 20, 2009 to continue the discussion of architectural constraints. This requirement is needed by the project stakeholders who must coordinate and document architecture decisions through a formal review cadence.
requirements.priority_rationale: A structured architecture review process is beneficial for coordinating architectural constraints, but it is not described as mandatory for system acceptability or compliance.

requirements.name: Interview-Based Requirements Intake
requirements.description: The system shall base its requirements on interviews with staff at member libraries conducted by working group members. Each member shall conduct at least one interview with staff at their library system to gather report needs, with the interviews due by April 15, 2009. This ensures the requirements are informed by member library report needs and that stakeholders have a shared basis for subsequent requirements work.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is important for deriving correct report needs from member libraries, but it is marked as proposed with a dated deliverable rather than an explicit mandatory requirement.

requirements.name: Vendor Website Interface Support
requirements.description: The system shall interface with vendor websites using published APIs and/or automated transfer of standard-format data files. The supported data file formats shall include USMARC21 and EDIFACT. This capability shall enable Management Processes to connect to a variety of vendor websites through approved integration mechanisms. This requirement is needed by the technical subcommittee stakeholders to ensure interoperability with external vendors and to support automated data exchange.
requirements.priority_rationale: Interfacing with vendor websites is essential for Management Processes to integrate and exchange data with external systems.

requirements.name: Indirect OPAC Patron Access
requirements.description: The system shall provide only indirect Patron access through OPAC displays, ensuring that Patrons are not direct Users of the Library Automation System. Any Patron interaction with system functionality shall occur via OPAC views rather than through authenticated staff or administrative system functions. This access boundary is required to enforce the separation between Patron-facing discovery/requests and protected system operations, supporting overall security and alignment of access behaviors across the consortium.
requirements.priority_rationale: This constraint is essential to prevent unauthorized direct system use by Patrons and to establish a secure access boundary for the OPAC experience.

requirements.name: Patron Data Availability for Reports
requirements.description: The system shall make patron fields available to reporting, including id, barcode, family_lib, usr_grp, email, address, birth_date, and create_date. For reporting purposes, address shall be composed of address lines, city, state, and zip (postal code). The system shall include family_lib as the home library and usr_grp as the patron type. The system shall include email as the em field and shall provide create_date and birth_date for patron records. This requirement is needed by stakeholders who develop or configure reports that rely on patron identifiers and key patron attributes for querying and aggregation.
requirements.priority_rationale: Patron fields are mandatory source data for creating and running patron-related reports.

requirements.name: Staff Role and Permission Administration
requirements.description: The system shall provide easy administration of roles and permissions, ensuring that administrative tasks are simple and straightforward. This capability supports Security & Access stakeholders who need roles and permissions to be maintained efficiently and correctly.
requirements.priority_rationale: Although important for secure operations and day-to-day administration, it is not explicitly stated as legally mandatory or required for initial usability.

requirements.name: Report Delivery Recipient Address Book
requirements.description: The system shall provide an address book for report delivery destinations, supporting delivery methods such as email and FTP. The address book shall store and manage the destinations used when delivering reports to recipients. This enables staff to configure report delivery destinations without lacking a central destination list. This requirement is needed by stakeholders responsible for reporting operations and report delivery setup.
requirements.priority_rationale: An address book is important for usable report delivery configuration, but the system could be workable initially with limited destination handling despite the identified gap.

requirements.name: Metadata Last-Edit Date Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall display a last-edit date on item reports that reflects the most recent metadata edit. The last-edit date displayed in the report shall exclude any circulation activity so that the value is not affected by circulation events. This requirement is needed by stakeholders who require visibility into when an Item’s metadata was last changed for accurate reporting and review.
requirements.priority_rationale: Displaying an accurate metadata last-edit date on item reports is essential for meeting stakeholders’ expectations of correct report content.

requirements.name: Last Circulation Date Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall include a field indicating last circulation date for items that is separate from last edit date. The system shall provide an indicator of the last circulation date on item reports. This capability is needed by stakeholders who require item reporting to reflect the most recent circulation rather than the most recent metadata edit.
requirements.priority_rationale: Last circulation date on item reports is important for accurate item usage reporting, but it can be deferred if circulation reporting is otherwise acceptable without a dedicated separate field in the initial release.

requirements.name: Exclude Renewals from Check-In
requirements.description: The system shall record check-in date/time separately from renewal timestamps so that check-in excludes renewals. The system shall ensure check-in date/time values shown in reports do not include renewals unless explicitly requested. This requirement ensures reporting accuracy for stakeholders who rely on correct separation between check-in events and renewal events, preventing renewals from inflating or contaminating check-in reporting.
requirements.priority_rationale: Accurate check-in timing in reports is important for reliable circulation reporting, but the system may still be usable with a workaround while the explicit separation is implemented.

requirements.name: Track Material Volume Report Requirement
requirements.description: The system shall record and track the Material Volume Report requirement as a key requirement within the project's requirements tracker. The system shall ensure this requirement is included in the tracker as an explicitly maintained key requirement. This requirement is needed by stakeholders responsible for maintaining and monitoring project requirements through the requirements tracker process.
requirements.priority_rationale: Because the source is agreed and explicitly states the Material Volume Report requirement must be tracked as a key requirement, it is essential for acceptable requirements maintenance.

requirements.name: Centralized Capacity Data Assumption
requirements.description: The system shall assume that capacity-related data is centralized in the system database unless analysis shows otherwise. The system shall use the centralized database as the basis for aggregating capacity data across all Library Automation System branches by querying that database. This requirement is needed to establish a common operating assumption and data access approach for stakeholders defining capacity analysis and reporting across the consortium.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is an important operating-environment assumption to support cross-branch capacity aggregation, but it is qualified by “unless analysis shows otherwise.”

requirements.name: Periodic Missing Item Reports
requirements.description: The system shall generate periodic reports of missing items for each Library or system scope. Each generated report shall include Missing items data aggregated by the selected scope (per branch/Library or system). This requirement ensures stakeholders can consistently monitor missing items over time using scheduled Reporting outputs rather than ad hoc queries, supporting operational oversight for Libraries and consortium administration.
requirements.priority_rationale: Periodic reporting of missing items is important for ongoing oversight, but it can be deferred if initial releases provide only on-demand missing-item reporting.

requirements.name: Items by Fines-Stopped Reason Reports
requirements.description: The system shall generate a Report listing Items by fines stopped reason. The report shall be provided as a list grouped or organized according to the fines stopped reason, using the “Items by Fines Stopped Reason” reporting content defined in the requirements evidence. This capability is needed by stakeholders who require visibility into which Items are associated with specific fines stopped reasons for reporting and analysis of financial outcomes tied to Items.
requirements.priority_rationale: This reporting is important for fine-related operational visibility but is not stated as mandatory (sources are only “proposed”), so it can be deferred if necessary.

requirements.name: Canned Missing Status Report
requirements.description: The system shall include a canned report listing Items with Missing Status. This canned Report shall present the set of Items where Missing Status applies, as part of the system’s standard reporting offerings. This requirement supports staff and administrators who need a repeatable way to identify and review Items with Missing Status without building a custom query each time.
requirements.priority_rationale: A canned report for Items with Missing Status is important for routine data review and reduces effort, but it is still usable if deferred while core reporting capabilities are delivered first.

requirements.name: Weeding Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide weeding reports to assist branch staff in collection maintenance. These reports are intended to be used frequently, supporting ongoing branch activities related to deciding what materials to weed. The functionality is needed by branch staff to maintain collection quality and support collection maintenance processes.
requirements.priority_rationale: Weeding reports are expected to support regular branch collection maintenance, but the requirement does not indicate they are mandatory for initial system acceptability.

requirements.name: WorldCat Last-Copy Workflow Support
requirements.description: The system shall support integration or workflow aids with WorldCat so catalogers can edit external bibliographic records for last-copy items. This support is intended to complement the system’s last-copy workflow by enabling catalogers to perform the required external record updates. The last-copy report and WorldCat integration are considered critical to enable this catalog maintenance work. This requirement is needed by catalogers and cataloging operations that rely on timely and accurate external bibliographic updates.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is important for catalogers’ last-copy operations via WorldCat editing, but its implementation details and system boundary relative to core cataloging responsibilities should be confirmed.

requirements.name: Catalog Cleanup Performance
requirements.description: The system shall provide cleanup tools and operations to reduce the time required to process orphaned records and other catalog cleanup cases. The system shall support performing cleanup using automated or assisted operations rather than requiring long manual processing by staff. This requirement is needed by cataloging stakeholders to improve staff efficiency when maintaining catalog data consistency. It addresses current pain points where cleaning up orphaned records “takes forever,” ensuring that cleanup operations complete in a timely manner without excessive manual effort.
requirements.priority_rationale: Improving catalog cleanup throughput is important for cataloging productivity, but the statement does not specify measurable response or throughput targets, so it is not mandatory for initial acceptability.

requirements.name: Administrative Candidate Material Queries
requirements.description: The system shall provide an administrative query function that identifies candidate materials for purposes such as selection or weeding. The query function shall be able to return candidate material results that can be used to support administrative decision-making. This capability is needed by administrative staff to efficiently locate and assess candidate materials during curation and weeding workflows.
requirements.priority_rationale: It is an important administrative reporting capability for selection/weeding workflows, but it is not explicitly described as mandatory for initial system acceptability.

requirements.name: Administrative Query Result Selection
requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to manually select items from query results for further actions. The system shall support manual selection of items originating from query results so administrators can choose a subset for subsequent processing. This capability is needed to support administrative workflows that require human selection rather than fully automated query output. It is especially relevant to administrators performing targeted actions based on the contents of a generated query result set.
requirements.priority_rationale: Administrators need a way to target specific items from query results for subsequent actions, but the system can still be usable without manual selection as long as an alternative selection workflow exists.

requirements.name: Missing MARC Field Bibliographic Reports
requirements.description: The system shall generate reports listing bibliographic records that are missing specified MARC fields. The report shall be based on identified MARC field criteria, producing a listing of bibliographic records that do not contain those fields. This capability supports stakeholders who need data quality and metadata completeness visibility for bibliographic records. It is needed by reporting stakeholders who require a consolidated view of MARC field omissions across the catalog data.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is an important reporting function for metadata quality, but it is described only as “proposed” with no explicit mandate, making it suitable for an expected release rather than strictly required first.

requirements.name: Acquisition Date Used for Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall use each Item’s acquisition date stored in the database to compute acquisition-based Reports and date-window queries. This acquisition date data assumption ensures that reporting and query logic can be driven by the database field rather than external inputs. Stakeholders needing this are reporting consumers and system operators who rely on consistent acquisition-date reporting across the environment.
requirements.priority_rationale: Acquisition-date-driven Reports and date-window queries depend on the database containing acquisition dates for Items, making it essential for acceptable reporting behavior.

requirements.name: Data Quality Issue Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide data quality reports that identify items with invalid item types, items with long call numbers, and bibliographic records with no item records. The system shall provide these data quality reports to help staff assess and correct data issues. The reports shall support data quality assessment by surfacing the specific data conditions of invalid item type, call number length, and missing associated item records for bibliographic records. This requirement is needed by staff who require actionable visibility into catalog data problems to correct them.
requirements.priority_rationale: Staff need data quality reports to assess and correct catalog issues, but the system may still be usable without this capability in an initial release.

requirements.name: Overview Display Large-Count Investigation
requirements.description: The system shall investigate technical constraints and report findings for displaying a large number of Libraries (286) in the overview. This investigation shall consider how the overview handles rendering and performance implications associated with that number of Libraries. The findings shall be documented as part of the project’s documentation work. This requirement is needed to help stakeholders understand feasibility and technical limitations before implementing the overview display for the expected scale.
requirements.priority_rationale: An investigation and documented findings are important for implementing the overview at the required scale, but the system could be workable initially with follow-on refinement once constraints are understood.

requirements.name: In-Transit Data Availability Assumption
requirements.description: The system shall assume it currently tracks Item status values such as "missing" and "long overdue" and that it maintains a transit table including arrival and departure dates. This assumption underpins any processing that relies on in-transit tracking data being available for Items during operation. It is needed so stakeholders can plan system behavior and data dependencies based on the existing system’s capabilities.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is an agreed operating-environment assumption that must hold for in-transit tracking and any dependent functions to operate correctly.

discarded.name: Branch-manager testing coordination assignment
discarded.explanation: Assigning a named individual to coordinate rollout and testing is a project-management responsibility, not a system requirement.

discarded.name: Shelf-space estimation investigation assignment
discarded.explanation: Assigning a named individual to investigate estimation methods is a project-management responsibility, not a product requirement. The implementable shelf-space estimation capability remains in K018.

discarded.name: Deletion-trigger implementation assignment
discarded.explanation: Assigning a named individual to provide a database trigger belongs in a project plan or responsibility matrix, not the product requirements specification.

discarded.name: Deletion-report drafting assignment
discarded.explanation: Assigning a named individual to draft detailed report requirements belongs in a project plan or responsibility matrix, not the product requirements specification.
